# Workforce Planning Management — documentation index

Workforce Planning Management (WPM) is an all-in-one HR platform for the
employee lifecycle, hire to retire, written as demonstration software with
synthetic data only. This page is the way in to its documents; it is also the
home page of the documentation site
([`workforce-planning-management.github.io/`](workforce-planning-management.github.io/README.md)).

> ⚠️ **Demo software.** Not a production HR or payroll system. See
> [spec/regulatory.md](spec/regulatory.md).

## Start here

- **[README.md](README.md)**: what WPM is, its status, the subprojects and how
  to run them.
- **[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)**: install, build and test, step by step.
- **[The family bridges tutorial](docs/tutorials/family-bridges.md)**: seven
  steps with `curl` through the bridges to the sibling project-portfolio-management
  and contact-relationship-management apps.

## The specification

- **[spec/index.md](spec/index.md)**: the single source of truth, its topic
  files and the requirements, design decisions and tasks.
- **[spec/worldwide.md](spec/worldwide.md)**: the target is worldwide, not the
  US or the UK; jurisdiction is data, and every locale is equal.
- **[spec/readiness-assessment.md](spec/readiness-assessment.md)**: the
  verdict for a high-assurance organization (not ready for production use).

## Role briefs

A page for each chief role and for governance, risk and compliance, in 21
locales: start with the [English source](locales/en-gb-oxendict/for/index.md)
or the [World English](locales/en-001/for/index.md) list, and see
[locales-x-for-roles](spec/locales-x-for-roles/index.md) for how they are
written. Every translation was written by an AI assistant and has not been
reviewed by a native speaker.

## The subprojects

- [The service](workforce-planning-management-service-with-rust/index.md): the
  Rust JSON API.
- [The UI](workforce-planning-management-ui-with-svelte/index.md): the
  SvelteKit client.
- [The matcher](workforce-planning-management-matcher-with-rust/README.md): the
  worker-record matcher crate.

## For contributors and agents

[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md),
[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md), [NEWS.md](NEWS.md) and [llms.txt](llms.txt).

# Workforce Planning Management (WPM)

An **all-in-one HR platform** demonstrating the employee lifecycle
hire to retire: talent acquisition & onboarding, workforce management
(time, leave, scheduling, the on-call rota), HR service delivery (employee
record and directory, org chart, self-service, benefits, wellbeing,
ergonomics, subject rights), talent management & development (reviews, 360°s,
training, skills gaps and training time, succession), strategic workforce
planning, joiners and leavers, announcements, a one-screen CEO dashboard, and
payroll & compensation — in **17 locales**. See
[spec/index.md](spec/index.md) for the full specification.

> ⚠️ **Demo software.** Not a production HR or payroll system;
> statutory calculations are illustrative stubs; no real personal
> data anywhere in the repository. See
> [spec/regulatory.md](spec/regulatory.md).

**Status (2026-10-30):** the demonstration was implemented through WPM-T97 (2026-07-18 to
2026-10-07); since then production readiness, operations and information governance, delivery
capacity, programmes and the contingent workforce, SFIA, unions, self-service, regulatory reporting,
outbound webhooks, the [cross-app bridges](spec/cross-app-bridges.md) to the sibling
project-portfolio-management and contact-relationship-management apps, and the first
[worldwide](spec/worldwide.md) tasks have been built. Much is still proposed or part done: see
[spec/tasks.md](spec/tasks.md) and the generated counts in
[spec/implementation-status.md](spec/implementation-status.md). Verified on 2026-10-30, on a
throwaway PostgreSQL 18 database: 1,040 service unit tests, 185 database-backed request tests and
every enforcement, security, retention, request-log, chaos and inventory binary; the UI's lint,
svelte-check, 291 unit tests and 325 Playwright tests over a stubbed API (19 skipped). Not rerun on
that date: the Keycloak and Entra suites (CI runs them), the Redis-backed shared-cache tests (no Redis
here), and the live Playwright specs against a real service. See each subproject's README and
[spec/testing.md](spec/testing.md).

## Subprojects

| Subproject | Role | Stack |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [workforce-planning-management-service-with-rust](workforce-planning-management-service-with-rust/) | Back-end JSON API | Rust, Loco (Axum + SeaORM), PostgreSQL |
| [workforce-planning-management-ui-with-svelte](workforce-planning-management-ui-with-svelte/) | HR / manager / self-service UI | SvelteKit 3, Svelte 5 runes, TypeScript |
| [workforce-planning-management-matcher-with-rust](workforce-planning-management-matcher-with-rust/) | Worker-record matcher crate (published; the service uses the crates.io copy) | Rust, no database, no clock |

Each subproject is self-contained: it owns its own `README.md`,
`AGENTS.md` (working agreements), `CHANGELOG.md`, and `spec/`
(stack-specific detail; the cross-cutting specification lives at the
repo root in [spec/](spec/)).

WPM is a **consumer application**: it does not register identities
itself. A person is a `person-service` record, their professional
identity a `worker-service` record, the employer an
`organization-service` record; training courses live in
`course-service`. WPM owns only the employment relationship and its
operational state, referencing identities by `EntityRef` URN, never
duplicating them. See [spec/scope.md](spec/scope.md) and
[spec/integrations.md](spec/integrations.md).

## Running

```sh
# Back-end
cd workforce-planning-management-service-with-rust
cargo run -- db migrate && cargo run -- task seed
WPM_REQUIRE_AUTH=0 cargo run -- start   # sign-in is enforced by default; this opts out for local use only

# Front-end (in another shell)
cd workforce-planning-management-ui-with-svelte
pnpm install && pnpm dev
```

See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for prerequisites and the full build/test
commands.

## What it does

| Area | Highlights |
| --- | --- |
| Hiring and the record | requisitions, applicant pipeline, onboarding, worker records, org chart, reporting lines, groups |
| Workforce | time and leave, shifts with working-time guardrails, **the on-call rota** (swaps, reminders), emergency contacts, **backups**, **the directory** |
| Development | reviews, 360°s, assessments, learning, CPD, **skills gap analysis**, **training time recommendations**, succession |
| Leadership | strategic workforce planning, metrics and **insights**, **a CEO dashboard on one iPad screen** |
| Joiners and leavers | dated checklists; a leaver's **last-day handover** with an audit trail |
| Communication | **announcements** with audiences, links and read counts |
| Rights and wellbeing | wellbeing prompts, the anonymous pulse, adjustments, subject access / erasure / retention |
| Global | 17 content locales at `/en-001/`, `/cy-001/`, … each at its one full-code address; strings edited through Sveltia CMS |

Design stance (see [spec/index.md](spec/index.md)): what must not be stored gets
no column; what must not be disclosed gets no endpoint; an unknown is never a
zero; roll-ups name no one; every estimate says what it rests on.

## Specification-driven delivery (SDD)

Three lock-step files drive delivery: [spec/requirements.md](spec/requirements.md)
(`WPM-R*`), [spec/design.md](spec/design.md) (`WPM-D*`), and
[spec/tasks.md](spec/tasks.md) — the live delivery checklist (`WPM-T*`).
A change starts in `requirements.md`, is shaped in `design.md`, is
queued in `tasks.md`, and only then lands as code. **No code lands
without the spec describing it.**

## Documentation

- [spec/index.md](spec/index.md) — the cross-cutting specification
  (purpose, scope, domain model, the five pillars, the newer topic files,
  auth, audit, architecture, testing, regulatory posture, roadmap, glossary).
- [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) — build, run, test, schedule the tasks, edit
  translations.
- [docs/tutorials/family-bridges.md](docs/tutorials/family-bridges.md) — a
  worked tour of the bridges to the sibling apps (pool link, peer demand and
  supply, people impact, the hire and leave webhooks, the overlap check, the
  lean worker list). [NEWS.md](NEWS.md), [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md),
  [COMPARISONS.md](COMPARISONS.md), [BENCHMARKS.md](BENCHMARKS.md).
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and [AGENTS/](AGENTS/spec-driven-delivery.md) — working
  agreements for humans and AI agents (spec-driven delivery, backend, frontend,
  privacy and data rules, localization, testing, git, docs).
- [llms.txt](llms.txt) and [llms.json](llms.json) — a map of this repository
  for AI agents.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — ground rules and how to
  contribute.
- [AI_STATEMENT.md](AI_STATEMENT.md) — how AI tools are used to
  develop this software.

## License

See [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md) (texts in [LICENSE/](LICENSE/index.md)). Each subproject declares its own SPDX
license expression in its manifest.

# Install

How to build and run both WPM subprojects from source.

## Try the demo (a guided tour with fictitious data)

The demo needs a **separate** service instance that holds nothing real, because it runs with authentication
off. In the service directory: create an empty database, `cargo run -- db migrate`, `cargo run -- task seed`,
start it with `WPM_REQUIRE_AUTH=0` (and, since a tour clicks quickly, `WPM_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=6000`), then
fill it from the repository root:

```sh
python3 scripts/demo-data.py http://localhost:5150
```

Start the UI with `WPM_DEMO_API_URL=http://localhost:5150`. On the sign-in page, sign in as
**example@example.com** (no email is sent): you land on `/demo`, a tour of every page, and a banner on each
page says the data is fictitious and offers Previous and Next. With `WPM_DEMO_API_URL` unset there is no
demo and that address signs in like any other. Never point `WPM_DEMO_API_URL` at a service that holds real
data: a demo session reaches only that service, with no authentication.

## Prerequisites

- **Rust** — stable. The service declares `rust-version = "1.99"` in
  `workforce-planning-management-service-with-rust/Cargo.toml`; the matcher, the migration
  crate and `entity-ref` declare 1.97, the project's N-2 policy (see WPM-T390 for why the
  service is not there yet).
- **Podman** (not Docker) — for the service's test database and Redis.
- **PostgreSQL 18 and Redis 8** — provided by
  `workforce-planning-management-service-with-rust/compose.test.yaml`;
  no host install needed for development.
- **Node.js 26** and **pnpm** — for the SvelteKit front-end
  (`"engines": { "node": "=26" }` in its `package.json`).

## Build and run the service

```sh
cd workforce-planning-management-service-with-rust
cargo run -- db migrate    # apply migrations
cargo run -- task seed     # synthetic orgs: ~40 employees paid in GBP, 3 in JPY
WPM_REQUIRE_AUTH=0 cargo run -- start   # JSON API, port 5150; sign-in enforcement is on by default,
                                         # so local development without an identity service opts out
```

```sh
cargo test --lib           # DB-free unit tests (1,034 on 2026-10-30)
cargo test --test mod -- --ignored --test-threads=1   # request tests (184; needs Postgres — see below)
cargo test --test enforcement -- --ignored --test-threads=1   # auth persona matrix
```

### Schedule the tasks

Several loco tasks do nothing unless something runs them. The job list is
[`config/scheduler.yaml`](workforce-planning-management-service-with-rust/config/scheduler.yaml), for Loco's own scheduler;
start **one** next to the server:

```sh
cargo loco scheduler --config config/scheduler.yaml --tag wpm     # webhooks, headcount snapshot, warnings, reminders, audit-chain check
cargo loco scheduler --config config/scheduler.yaml --tag scim    # only where WPM_SCIM_BASE_URL and WPM_SCIM_TOKEN are set
cargo loco scheduler --config config/scheduler.yaml --list        # what is scheduled, and when
```

Or schedule the same tasks yourself (cron, a systemd timer, a Kubernetes CronJob) with `cargo run -- task <name>`; the table in
[spec/operations/deployment.md](spec/operations/deployment.md) says how often each one wants to run.

Optional imports: `cargo run -- task import_framework` (UK GDAD PCF) and
`import_esco` (ESCO occupations and skills) — see the task entries in
[spec/tasks.md](spec/tasks.md) for the data files they read.

## Run the service's DB-gated tests

```sh
podman compose -f compose.test.yaml up -d --wait
export WPM_TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379   # the Redis-backed tests skip without it
cargo test --test mod -- --ignored --test-threads=1   # serial: the tests share one database
podman compose -f compose.test.yaml down
```

## Build and run the front-end

```sh
cd workforce-planning-management-ui-with-svelte
cp .env.example .env       # WPM_API_URL / AUTH_API_URL — both default
                            # to http://localhost:5150
pnpm install
pnpm dev                   # expects the service running (stub mode is fine)
```

```sh
pnpm lint                  # eslint, then prettier --check
pnpm check                 # svelte-kit sync && svelte-check
pnpm test                  # vitest (291 on 2026-10-30)
pnpm exec playwright test  # 335 pass, 19 skip; page.route-stubbed, no running service needed
                           # (PW_PORT=<free port> if 4173 is taken)
pnpm build
```

Open `http://localhost:5173/` — it redirects to your locale, e.g.
`/en-001/`. Every page is served under its locale (`/cy-001/workers`); `/en/…`
redirects to `/en-001/…`.

### Edit the translations

The UI strings are content: `content/locales/<locale>/ui.json`. Edit them in a
file, or in the browser with Sveltia CMS at `/<locale>/admin/` (it signs in with
GitHub and commits to the repository). After adding a key to `en-001`, add it to
every other `-001` locale and run `pnpm cms-config` to regenerate
`static/admin/config.yml`; the tests fail if either is missed.

### The CEO dashboard

`/ceo` is built for one screen: an iPad (9th generation), 2160 × 1620 pixels =
1080 × 810 CSS pixels at 2×. In Chrome DevTools use a custom device of 1080 × 810
with a device pixel ratio of 2 to see it as intended.

## Run the demo in containers

From a fresh clone, with no sibling repositories:

```sh
podman compose up --build
curl http://localhost:5150/_health
```

This starts PostgreSQL, Redis, a demo mail server (Stalwart: a catch-all for `wpm.test` that delivers nothing
outside; read it with `python3 scripts/demo-mailbox.py`) and the API. **It turns sign-in enforcement off**
(`WPM_REQUIRE_AUTH: "0"` in `compose.yaml`, with a warning in the log) because
the demo has no identity service; use synthetic data only. The UI is not
containerized. Not yet verified: the image build, because the maintainer's
machine could not pull base images when this was written.

## Running the service tests

`entity-ref` is vendored in `workforce-planning-management-service-with-rust/crates/`
and `authentication-verifier` comes from crates.io, so a fresh clone builds and tests
on its own. Start a throwaway Postgres and Redis and run the suites (the request
suite runs serially, and each of the other test binaries in its own process):

```sh
cd workforce-planning-management-service-with-rust
podman compose -f compose.test.yaml up -d --wait
export WPM_TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379   # Postgres on 5432, Redis on 6379; both have port overrides
cargo test                                   # unit tests, no database
cargo test --test mod -- --ignored --test-threads=1
cargo test --test enforcement -- --ignored --test-threads=1
cargo test --test enforcement_expenses -- --ignored --test-threads=1
cargo test --test security -- --ignored --test-threads=1
cargo test --test chaos -- --ignored --nocapture   # database faults; WPM_CHAOS_SEED=<n> replays a run
scripts/verify-db-roles.sh                         # the request tests as the least-privilege role (postgres-roles/roles.sql); a few minutes
podman compose -f compose.test.yaml down
```

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the same commands and every other enforcement
binary, plus `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo deny`, the MSRV check, the
Keycloak and Entra suites, the front-end checks and Playwright.

## Try the family bridges

[docs/tutorials/family-bridges.md](docs/tutorials/family-bridges.md) walks through every bridge to
the sibling apps with `curl` against a throwaway service.

## Auth

The service enforces sign-in **by default** (`WPM_REQUIRE_AUTH`; only an
explicit `0` disables it, and `production` refuses to start that way). See
[spec/auth.md](spec/auth.md) to point it at your token keys and mount a real
ABAC policy, and
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) before exposing either subproject to
untrusted callers.

# Tutorial: the family bridges

How WPM talks to its two siblings, **project-portfolio-management (PPM)** and
**contact-relationship-management (CRM)**, one bridge at a time. Each step is a
`curl` against a local service; the rules behind each one are in
[spec/cross-app-bridges.md](../../spec/cross-app-bridges.md) (WPM-R206 to
WPM-R216, WPM-D134 to WPM-D147).

> ⚠️ **Demo software.** Synthetic data only. See
> [spec/regulatory.md](../../spec/regulatory.md).

Every bridge carries **references and counts, never records** (WPM-D134), and
every inbound call acts **under the caller's own token** (WPM-D135). Here
sign-in is turned off, so no token is sent; in a real deployment PPM and CRM
forward their user's `Authorization: Bearer` token, and WPM's policy decides
exactly as it does for that user on the same route.

**What this tutorial does not show.** PPM's sender and puller and CRM's webhook
receiver and import are built by their owners and have not been run against
WPM; here `curl` plays both siblings.

## 0. Start a throwaway service

You need PostgreSQL, Rust, `jq` and `uuidgen` (see [INSTALL.md](../../INSTALL.md)).
Use an empty database that holds nothing real, because sign-in is off:

```sh
cd workforce-planning-management-service-with-rust
export DATABASE_URL=postgres://localhost:5432/wpm_tutorial   # an empty database
cargo run -- db migrate
export WPM_REQUIRE_AUTH=0                   # never on a service that holds real data
export WPM_WEBHOOK_SECRET_CRM=tutorial-only-secret
cargo run -- start &                        # the API on :5150
```

In another shell, make an organization reference and a few workers in one
department (the person references are made up here; in the family they are
person-service records). A worker created by HR starts `onboarding`; the
function makes each one `active`:

```sh
API=localhost:5150/api
ORG="organization:$(uuidgen | tr A-Z a-z)"
hire() {  # hire <worker number> -> prints the worker's pid
  local pid
  pid=$(curl -s $API/workers -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
    "person_ref": "person:'$(uuidgen | tr A-Z a-z)'", "organization_ref": "'$ORG'",
    "worker_number": "'$1'", "display_name": "Tutorial '$1'",
    "employment_type": "permanent", "department": "tutorial",
    "job_title": "Engineer", "salary_minor": 3600000, "salary_currency": "GBP",
    "hired_on": "2026-01-05" }' | jq -r .pid)
  curl -s $API/workers/$pid/status -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"to": "active"}' >/dev/null
  echo $pid
}
ADA=$(hire T-1); hire T-2 >/dev/null; hire T-3 >/dev/null
ADA_PERSON=$(curl -s $API/workers/$ADA | jq -r .person_ref)
```

## 1. Link a pool to PPM's pool (WPM-R213, WPM-D139)

A skill pool is WPM's; the link to PPM's pool for the same skills is set by a
person, by id, never matched by name. PPM holds the WPM pool's pid in its own
`peer_pool_ref`.

```sh
POOL=$(curl -s $API/skill-pools -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"organization_ref": "'$ORG'", "name": "Tutorial engineers"}' | jq -r .pid)
PPM_POOL=$(uuidgen | tr A-Z a-z)            # PPM's pool pid, as PPM shows it
curl -s -X PUT $API/skill-pools/$POOL/peer-link -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"peer_pool_ref": "'$PPM_POOL'"}' | jq '{peer_pool_ref, demand_source}'
```

A linked pool counts PPM's demand and ignores what was entered here (one owner
per fact, WPM-D140). Until PPM sends a figure, its demand is **unknown**, not
zero (WPM-D141). `{"peer_pool_ref": null}` removes the link and the local
figures count again at once.

## 2. PPM sends demand; WPM gives supply (WPM-R210, WPM-R215)

PPM names its plan as a `thing:` reference to the plan's pid. A figure is in
hundredths of an FTE for the first day of a month, with PPM's own event id.
An event id is a repeat only for the same pool, programme and month: the same
id for another pool, programme or month is a new event there (WPM-D148). Here
each run makes its own:

```sh
PLAN="thing:$(uuidgen | tr A-Z a-z)"
MONTH=$(date +%Y-%m-01)
EV=$(uuidgen | tr A-Z a-z)                  # a prefix for this run's event ids
demand() {  # demand <fte_centi> <event id> <sent_at>
  curl -s $API/capacity/peer-demand -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
    "pool_pid": "'$POOL'", "programme_ref": "'$PLAN'", "month": "'$MONTH'",
    "fte_centi": '$1', "peer_event_id": "'$2'", "sent_at": "'$3'" }' | jq -c .
}
demand 150 $EV-1 2026-10-30T10:00:00Z   # {"duplicate":false,"outcome":"recorded",...,"status":"proposed"}
demand 150 $EV-1 2026-10-30T10:00:00Z   # the same event again: duplicate, nothing changes
demand 120 $EV-0 2026-10-30T09:00:00Z   # sent before $EV-1: "stale", ignored
demand 0   $EV-2 2026-10-30T11:00:00Z   # zero withdraws it: "withdrawn", status "closed"
curl -s "$API/programme-demands?pool=$POOL" | jq '.[] | {source, status, fte_centi, peer_sent_at, peer_withdrawn_at}'
```

A received claim arrives `proposed` and counts only after a person's start
decision (WPM-D50); a withdrawal never undoes that decision. The full table of
outcomes is in [cross-app-bridges.md](../../spec/cross-app-bridges.md), WPM-R215.

PPM pulls the pool's supply, by month, in hundredths of an FTE. A month made up
of one to four workers is hidden (`supply_centi: null`, `hidden: true`), and no
total is given:

```sh
curl -s "$API/capacity/peer-supply?pool=$POOL&months=3" | jq -c '.months[]'
# {"hidden":false,"month":"2026-10-01","supply_centi":0} ... one line a month
```

This pool names no role profile or skill, so nobody counts towards it and each
month is a known zero (zero is shown; it names no one). A pool's members come
from its role profiles and skills, as in the capacity view
([spec/delivery-capacity.md](../../spec/delivery-capacity.md)).

## 3. PPM asks for people impact (WPM-R211)

Counts only, for a programme: people committed to it by pool, contingent
engagements ending before the programme ends, and over-committed pool-months.
WPM holds no end date for a PPM plan, so PPM passes `ends_on`; without it that
part is unknown with a reason. A count under ten is hidden.

```sh
curl -s "$API/capacity/people-impact?programme=$PLAN&ends_on=2027-03-31" \
  | jq '{workers_committed: .workers_committed.known, reason: .workers_committed.reason,
         over: .over_committed_pool_months.over}'
```

Here no post is recorded as funded by the plan, so `workers_committed` is
unknown: WPM cannot tell "nobody" from "not recorded", and says so.

## 4. CRM hears of a hire or a leaver by webhook (WPM-R207, WPM-D145)

CRM subscribes an endpoint to the three kinds. The signing secret stays in the
service's environment; the subscription holds only its variable's name:

```sh
SUB=$(curl -s $API/webhook-subscriptions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "name": "crm-handoff", "url": "http://localhost:9999/wpm-events",
  "kinds": ["worker_hired", "worker_terminated", "worker_retired"],
  "secret_ref": "WPM_WEBHOOK_SECRET_CRM" }' | jq -r .pid)
NEW=$(hire T-4)
cargo run -- task webhook_deliver           # the scheduler runs this every minute
curl -s $API/webhook-subscriptions/$SUB/deliveries | jq -c '.[0] | {kind, status, attempts, last_error}'
# {"kind":"worker_hired","status":"pending","attempts":1,"last_error":"request failed"}
```

The delivery `POST`ed to the endpoint carries the handoff references and
nothing else: no name, department or pay.

```json
{ "id": "<event uuid>", "kind": "worker_hired", "subject": "worker:<pid>", "occurred_at": "…",
  "data": { "person_ref": "person:<uuid>", "organization_ref": "organization:<uuid>", "effective_on": "2026-01-05" } }
```

Nothing listens on port 9999 here, so the delivery stays `pending`, with its
error and the time of its next attempt (`next_attempt_at`), and is retried with
back-off. A receiver checks `x-wpm-signature` (`t=<unix>,v1=<hex
HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">`) and is idempotent on the event `id`, because
delivery is at least once.

## 5. CRM checks which of its contacts are workers (WPM-R208)

CRM already holds `person:` references. It may ask, for up to 500 of them,
which are workers of the organization today; the answer is a yes or no for each
and nothing more, and the audit entry holds counts, not references:

```sh
curl -s $API/bridges/overlap -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "organization_ref": "'$ORG'",
  "person_refs": ["'$ADA_PERSON'", "person:'$(uuidgen | tr A-Z a-z)'"] }' | jq -c '.results[]'
# {"person_ref":"person:…","worker":true}
# {"person_ref":"person:…","worker":false}
```

## 6. CRM's import asks for a lean worker list (WPM-R216, WPM-D147)

CRM's teams import needs three fields of each active worker. It names them, and
gets those and no others:

```sh
curl -s "$API/workers?status=active&fields=pid,department,person_ref&limit=200&offset=0" | jq -c '.[0]'
# {"department":"tutorial","person_ref":"person:…","pid":"…"}
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "$API/workers?fields=pid,nmae"   # an unknown name: 422
```

A list that carries a salary (no `fields`, or `fields` naming `salary_minor` or
`salary_currency`) records a `salary_read` audit entry for each worker whose
salary it shows unmasked, as the single-worker read does; the lean list above
records none.

## Clean up

Stop the service and drop the database (`dropdb wpm_tutorial`).

# Workforce Planning Management — Specification

This directory is the **single source of truth** for the cross-cutting
Workforce Planning Management (WPM) specification, shared by both editions.
Each subproject's own `spec/` adds stack-specific detail and links back
here.

> ⚠️ **Demo software, not a production HR system.** This project models
> WPM practice for demonstration and integration purposes. It is not
> a payroll system of record, not employment-law advice, and holds no
> real personal data. See [regulatory.md](regulatory.md).

## What this project is

An **all-in-one HR platform** managing an organization's workforce
through the whole employee lifecycle — hiring to retirement. Where
traditional HR software handles administrative record-keeping, WPM
adds **strategic workforce optimization and talent development**:

1. **Talent acquisition & onboarding** — requisitions, an applicant
   tracking pipeline, a candidate pool, digitized onboarding.
2. **Workforce management** — time & attendance, absence/leave,
   shift scheduling, advisory working-time guardrails.
3. **HR service delivery** — the employee record as the single source
   of employment truth, org charts, self-service, benefits, wellbeing
   & benefits-awareness prompts, the anonymous pulse, ergonomic (DSE)
   assessments, reasonable adjustments, in-app notifications, and
   subject rights (access / erasure / retention).
4. **Talent management & development** — performance reviews, 360°
   multi-rater appraisals, training via the family's course registry,
   assessments (aptitude / personality / psychometric / selection /
   cognitive), skills & learning paths, mentorships, development
   plans, talent pipelines, early careers, succession, workforce
   intelligence.
5. **Payroll & compensation** — payroll runs, payslips, salary
   benchmarking.

Cross-cutting capabilities added since the five pillars were first
delivered: **people & cover** (employee directory, emergency contacts,
backups, the on-call rota), **skills gaps and training time**,
**joiners and leavers** with a last-day handover, **announcements**, a
**CEO dashboard** and workforce insights, strategic workforce planning
(WPM-R34–R38), job-capability frameworks (UK GDAD PCF, ESCO), reporting
lines and groups, organization memberships and transfers, and
**17 content locales** (13 languages at `-001`, 4 regional) served under `/<locale>/` routes.

It is a **consumer application** (the case-folder / patient-flow /
project-portfolio-management shape): it does not register identities
itself. A human is a person-service
record; their professional identity is a
worker-service record; the
employer is an organization-service
record; training courses live in the
course-service. WPM owns only
the **employment relationship and its operational state**: employee
records, requisitions, applications, time, leave, shifts, benefits,
reviews, enrollments, succession, payroll — always referencing
identities by `EntityRef` URN, never duplicating them.

| [workforce-planning-management-ui-with-svelte](../workforce-planning-management-ui-with-svelte/) | HR / manager / self-service UI | SvelteKit 2, Svelte 5 runes, TypeScript |

## Specification-driven delivery (SDD)

Three lock-step files drive delivery:

- [requirements.md](requirements.md) — numbered requirements (`WPM-R*`)
  with user stories and acceptance criteria.
- [design.md](design.md) — numbered design decisions (`WPM-D*`).
- [tasks.md](tasks.md) — **the live delivery checklist** (`WPM-T*`),
  phased; every task traces to design and requirement ids.

A change starts in `requirements.md`, is shaped in `design.md`, is
queued in `tasks.md`, and only then lands as code in a subproject.
**No code lands without the spec describing it.**

**Status (2026-10-07):** tasks WPM-T1–T97 delivered (no open deferral;
expense claims, the last, is WPM-T97 in [tasks.md](tasks.md)); requirements WPM-R1–R55,
design decisions WPM-D1–D42. Current verification: 317 unit tests, 62 database-backed request
tests, the auth enforcement and Keycloak suites, 80 front-end unit tests and
45 Playwright specs — see [testing.md](testing.md).

The load-bearing design thread (decisions WPM-D17–D25, extended by
WPM-D29–D36): **what must
not be stored gets no column** (no health cohort, no symptom, no
diagnosis, no pulse author), **what must not be disclosed gets no
endpoint** (no rater-level 360 content, no per-adjustment reporting),
and **every limit is stated in the payload rather than hidden**
(derivation strings, named exclusions, `null`-not-zero rates,
k-floors that withhold their counts). Since WPM-T69 the same thread
runs through the newer surfaces: an undeclared skill is *unknown*, not a
shortfall (WPM-D32); a cover or on-call day with nobody available says so
(WPM-D31); a training recommendation states what it rests on (WPM-D33);
announcement read receipts are counts, never names (WPM-D35).

## References

- Sibling consumer apps (the shape this follows):
  patient-flow,
  case-folder,
  project-portfolio-management
- Family contracts: cross-service-linking
  (the `employed_by` worker→organization edge is a registry v1 kind),
  authentication-sessions,
  authorization-attributes,
  security

# Worldwide by design

*Added 2026-10-29 at the product owner's direction.*

WPM's target is the whole world, not the United States or the United Kingdom. Much of the current spec, the seed data and the
regulatory register was written with UK examples (UK GDPR, NHS-style pay scales, MHRA, `en-gb`). Those are **examples and the first
worked cases, not the design.** This file is the rule that stops them becoming the design.

## Requirement

- **WPM-R214** Every standard, protocol, convention, locale and the like that WPM adopts must have **equitable capability for countries,
  regions and federations worldwide**. No jurisdiction is the default, the first-class case or the only case that works; a deployer in
  any country, in a federation of states, or in a region spanning several countries can configure and run WPM without a code change and
  without a lesser experience than a UK or US deployer.

## Decision

- **WPM-D143 Jurisdiction is data, never code; a standard is adopted as a profile, never as the only shape.**
  *Proposed, needs product-owner confirmation* (drafted 2026-10-29 by the AI assistant from the instruction above).
  - **Jurisdictions are configuration.** Statutory rules (working-time limits, notice, leave, retention periods, pay-transparency,
    equality categories, data-protection regime) live in per-organization, per-jurisdiction data with an effective date, as pay scales
    and the SFIA import already do. A rule in `src/rules/` takes the jurisdiction's parameters as an input and names no country.
    UK values may ship as a worked example profile beside at least one non-UK profile of a different shape.
  - **Federations and regions are first-class.** A country is not the only unit: a federal state, province, canton, a supranational
    region (for example the EU) and a bloc with shared law are each representable, and a worker or organization may be under more than
    one layer (national and regional; the stricter or the more specific applies as the profile says).
  - **No Anglophone or Western default shapes.** Names (no first/last assumption; one full-name field plus optional parts), addresses,
    dates and calendars (more than Gregorian; week start and weekend days vary), numbers and currency (minor-unit exponent per ISO 4217,
    not always 2), time zones, phone formats, and identifiers (no assumed national-insurance or SSN shape) are all per-locale or
    per-jurisdiction. Equality and disability categories are configured per jurisdiction; none is hard-coded as the list.
  - **Standards: international first, national as profiles.** Prefer an international or open standard (ISO, IETF, W3C, Unicode CLDR,
    ILO conventions) where one exists, and add national or regional standards as profiles of it. Where the only available standard is
    national, say so in the entry and record what a deployer elsewhere does instead.
  - **Locales are equal.** A locale is complete or it is marked incomplete; no locale gets features another lacks. Right-to-left,
    non-Latin scripts, and plural and gender rules beyond English are supported (the 17 shipped locales include `ar-001`, `ur-001`,
    `hi-001`, `bn-001`, `zh-001`); additions follow [localization](../AGENTS/localization.md).
  - **Claims are scoped.** Where the spec says what a law requires, it names the jurisdiction. No sentence says "the law" or "statutory"
    without one. A jurisdiction not yet read is recorded as *not yet read*, as MHRA is, never assumed to match the UK.
  - **Equity is tested.** A change that adds a jurisdiction-specific rule is not done without the same rule's parameters being
    expressible for a second, differently shaped jurisdiction (a test with two profiles).

- **WPM-D144 Jurisdiction rules are held as dated, sourced profiles by jurisdiction code, resolved by one pure function.**
  *Confirmed by the product owner, 2026-10-31, as written in full* (questions 1 to 4 of the design were confirmed on 2026-10-29: the demo seed always loads example profiles; HR of the organization edits a profile; ISO 3166 plus a deployer-extended supranational list; a structured `work_jurisdiction` set by HR. Question 5 was answered "y" to the assistant's suggestion: the second example profile is India, then Japan, both labelled `example`/unverified. On 2026-10-31 the registry and resolver design itself was confirmed too). The design is in "Jurisdiction profile design" below: parameters with no default, layers
  (supranational, national, subnational) chained per organization, a combination rule per parameter, the applicable chain taken from the
  place the work is done, and append-only rows with a source and a status.

- **WPM-D149 A calendar's "today", week start and weekend are the reader's, from the browser, until a user or organization setting exists.**
  *Confirmed by the product owner, 2026-10-31* (drafted 2026-10-30 by the AI assistant for WPM-T378). The UI only; the API keeps ISO
  dates and is unchanged.
  - **Today** is the date in the reader's own time zone (the browser's `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`), never the
    UTC date: near midnight far from UTC the two differ by a day. A timestamp placed on a calendar day (a shift) is placed on its day in
    that zone. A civil date from the API ("2026-10-30") is the same day everywhere and is never shifted.
  - **Week start and weekend** come from Unicode CLDR week data through `Intl.Locale#getWeekInfo()` (or the older `weekInfo`
    property), for a region taken in this order: the page locale's own country (`en-us`, `de-de`); else the first country among the
    browser's languages (`navigator.languages`, so a reader in Egypt on `ar-001` gets Saturday and a Friday–Saturday weekend); else the
    page locale itself, whose `001` (world) region is Monday and Saturday–Sunday in CLDR. The language alone never chooses a country: an
    `ar-001` page with no country in the browser is *not* assumed to be Egyptian or Saudi.
  - **Fallback** where the browser has neither `getWeekInfo` nor `weekInfo`: a small table copied from CLDR `weekData` (Sunday-first,
    Saturday-first and Friday-first regions; Friday–Saturday, Thursday–Friday, Friday-only and Sunday-only weekends), else Monday and
    Saturday–Sunday (ISO 8601 and the CLDR world default). The table is a fallback, not the source; it may lag CLDR.
  - **Not decided here:** a stored user or organization time zone and region (D144's `work_jurisdiction` could supply the region); the
    service's own "today" (the server's clock) and the working-time and holiday rules' weekend (WPM-T379, WPM-T380).

- **WPM-D152 Addresses and telephone numbers keep what the person typed; their shape per country is a recorded choice.**
  *Confirmed by the product owner, 2026-10-31, with the answers below* (drafted 2026-10-30 by the AI assistant for WPM-T382). What
  WPM-T382 built (any-script phone digits, no postcode pattern, neutral labels) holds.
  - **The answers (2026-10-31).** **Question 1: (c), both.** The structured fields stay, with a per-country order and label table, and a
    free-text address block is the fallback for a country the table lacks. **Question 2: all three forms are kept.** A number is stored
    as typed; beside it as ASCII digits (for search and export); and as E.164 where it can be derived: the number was written with `+`,
    or its country is known (the address's country, else the worker's `work_jurisdiction` country). A country is never guessed, and
    where none of these holds the E.164 form is absent, not invented. **Question 3: the picker.** Names come from `Intl.DisplayNames` in
    the page's locale, the stored value is the ISO 3166-1 code, and a deployer may add a code ISO 3166-1 lacks (for example `XK`) from
    D144's supranational and deployer-extended list.
  - *As drafted, for the record:*
  - **Question 1, the address shape.** (a) Keep the structured fields (two lines, locality, region, postal code, country) and add a
    per-country order and label table (the shape of Google's libaddressinput data; CLDR has none), so a Japanese address is shown large
    to small and a US one with "State" and "ZIP Code"; or (b) one free-text address block plus the country, ordered by the person; or
    (c) both, the block as the fallback for a country the table lacks. The assistant's suggestion: (c), because payroll exports in some
    countries need the parts and no table covers every country.
  - **Question 2, telephone numbers.** (a) Stored as typed (today); (b) stored as typed and also as ASCII digits for search and export;
    or (c) normalised to E.164, which needs the country of a number written without `+` (D144's `work_jurisdiction`, not built). The
    assistant's suggestion: (b), so nothing the person typed is lost and no country is guessed.
  - **Question 3, the country field.** A picker whose names come from `Intl.DisplayNames` in the page's locale, still storing the ISO
    3166-1 code; and whether a deployer may add a code ISO 3166-1 lacks (`XK` for Kosovo is user-assigned). The assistant's suggestion:
    the picker, with the deployer's extra codes from D144's supranational list.

- **WPM-D151 A currency's minor unit is its ISO 4217 one, from one table the API and the UI share; the API refuses a code outside it.**
  *Confirmed by the product owner, 2026-10-31* (drafted 2026-10-30 by the AI assistant for WPM-T400, after the contact relationship
  management app's fix, its commit 37ef205, and the project portfolio management UI's, its commit 490ad5d).
  - **The stored unit is ISO 4217's.** An amount is an integer count of the currency's ISO 4217 minor unit: HUF, IDR, COP and PKR have 2
    decimal places, IQD 3, JPY 0, KWD 3, CLF 4. Unicode CLDR's *display* digits are not the minor unit: CLDR shows 0 places for 16 codes
    (AFN, ALL, COP, HUF, IDR, IQD, IRR, KPW, LAK, LBP, MGA, MMK, PKR, SOS, SYP, YER) where ISO 4217 has 2, or 3 for IQD. A UI that took the
    exponent from `Intl` (which uses CLDR) stored 1,500 forint as 1,500 fillér, a hundredth of the amount the API means.
  - **One table, two copies, held equal.** The service's `src/rules/currency.rs` (`MINOR_UNITS`, the shape of the sibling project
    portfolio management service's `src/currency.rs` and the contact relationship management service's `src/rules/currency.rs`) and the
    UI's `src/lib/money.ts` hold the same entries; a vitest test reads the Rust file and fails when they differ. `Intl` is the UI's
    fallback only for a code the table does not hold, and gives the number format (separators, symbol, digits) in every case.
  - **Shown, typed and stored in the same unit.** The UI formats with `minimumFractionDigits` and `maximumFractionDigits` set to the ISO
    exponent, so a forint amount shows two places ("Ft 1,500.50"), a whole one in `moneyWhole` shows none.
  - **The API accepts only codes in the table.** Where the API takes a currency (an expense claim, a worker's salary, a requisition's or a
    hire's salary, a contractor's rate, a plan budget, a benefit plan, a benchmark, a pay or cost query), a code that is not three capital
    letters in the table is refused with 422. Funds and metals with no minor unit (`XAU`, `XDR`, `XXX`) are not in it.
  - **Stored data is not rewritten.** An amount already stored is not rescaled by the service: it cannot tell a forint amount typed in
    the UI under WPM-T373 from one an API client sent in fillér. What an operator checks is in WPM-T400.

## Jurisdiction profile design (WPM-T368, 2026-10-29)

*Written as a design only (no code, migration or test changed by WPM-T368). WPM-D144; questions 1 to 4 below were answered yes by the
product owner on 2026-10-29 (HR edits), question 5 answered: India first, then Japan; the whole design was confirmed as written on
2026-10-31.*

### What exists today

A jurisdiction's rules reach WPM in four different ways, none of which can hold two jurisdictions at once:

| Way | Examples | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A **constant in code** | `working_time.rs`: 17 weeks, 48 hours, 11 hours of rest | One value for every deployment |
| A **deployment-wide setting** | `WPM_RETENTION_DAYS`, `WPM_PAY_INFORMATION_MONTHS`, `WPM_JOINT_ASSESSMENT_THRESHOLD_PERCENT`, `WPM_PAY_GAP_SEX_CATEGORY` | One value per deployment, so one country per deployment, and no date |
| **Rows with a region** | `holidays.region` (a code like `GB-ENG` or `US` or `DE`, checked against `^[A-Z0-9]{2,3}(-[A-Z0-9]{1,3})?$`) | Right shape, but only for holidays |
| **Reference data** | pay scales (WPM-T102), student loan thresholds, SFIA and ESCO imports | Dated and sourced, but keyed by nothing common |

### The model

A **profile** is a dated, sourced set of **parameters** for one **jurisdiction code**, held by an organization. Three nouns:

- **Jurisdiction code.** The shape the holidays already use, which is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 for a country, ISO 3166-2 for a subdivision (a
  state, province, canton, nation within a state) and a registered code for a supranational region (`EU`; others by a short list the
  deployer extends). A code has a **layer**: `supranational`, `national` or `subnational`. A code has a parent (`GB-ENG` → `GB`; `DE` → `EU`),
  so a federation, a bloc or a country of countries is just a chain. The chain is data, kept per organization, because membership changes
  (a state leaves a bloc) and WPM does not assert it.
- **Parameter.** A key from a **parameter registry** (a list in the spec, then in code): `working_time.max_average_weekly_minutes`,
  `working_time.reference_weeks`, `working_time.min_daily_rest_minutes`, `retention.<class>.days`, `pay_transparency.information_months`,
  `pay_transparency.joint_assessment_percent`, `holidays.weekend_days`, `calendar.week_start`, `equality.categories`, `deduction.<scheme>`,
  and so on. Each registry entry fixes its **type and unit**, its **combination rule** (below), and its **validation range**. A parameter
  has **no default value**: not configured is `unknown`, never a number (WPM-D141's rule, and the AGENTS rule that an unknown is never a zero).
- **Profile row.** `(organization, jurisdiction code, parameter key, value, effective_from, effective_to?, source, checked_on, status)`.
  `status` is `read` (the source was read and checked on that date), `example` (a worked case, as the UK values will be) or `unverified`.
  Rows are **append-only**: a change is a new row with a later `effective_from`, so a past decision can be explained by the rule in force
  that day, and the audit trail names the parameter and the code but no person and no figure about a person.

### Which jurisdictions apply to a worker

A worker is under the chain of the **place the work is done**, **not** nationality, citizenship, residence or any characteristic of the
person. This is the usual legal test for employment rules, and it keeps a protected characteristic out of the rules. **The staff record
cannot say this today:** `Worker.location` is free text (≤ 100 characters, [domain-model.md](domain-model.md)), so it cannot be resolved to a
code. The design therefore needs a new, structured, optional **`work_jurisdiction`** (a jurisdiction code) on the worker, set by HR, with the
free-text location left as it is. A remote worker's value is a fact about the assignment, set by HR. Where it is not set, the answer is
`unknown` and the guardrails say so; it is never defaulted to the organization's own country.

### How parameters combine across layers

Each registry entry names one rule, and the resolver is one pure function in `rules::jurisdiction`:

| Rule | Used for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `most_specific` | week start, weekend days, currency exponent | The deepest layer that has a value wins |
| `strictest_min` / `strictest_max` | a weekly-hours ceiling (the lowest value), a rest minimum (the highest value) | The most protective of all layers that apply |
| `union` | public holidays, equality categories | All layers' values together |
| `bounded` | retention (a floor from one law, a ceiling from another) | The intersection; an **empty intersection is refused and shown** to HR, not resolved silently |

`resolve(parameter, chain, as_of) -> Resolved { value, from_code, status, source } | Unknown`. It is DB-free and clock-free, tested with at
least two profiles of a different shape (T369). A result always says **where the value came from**, and every screen or report that
uses one shows it, as the capacity view shows its demand's source (WPM-D140).

### What changes in each existing area

| Area (audit row) | Today | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Working-time guardrails (5) | Constants, named for the Working Time Regulations | Three parameters; the UK/EU values are an `example` profile; with none configured the flags say `no limit configured`, not `no breach` |
| Retention (config) | One `WPM_RETENTION_*` per deployment | `bounded` parameters per class; the env var becomes a fallback for a deployment with no profile, until it is removed |
| Pay transparency (7) | `WPM_*` settings with the Directive's values | Parameters under `EU`; another region's regime is another profile, or absent |
| Student loans (3) | `StudentLoanPlan` with UK plan names | A general **statutory deduction scheme**: `(jurisdiction, scheme, code, period, threshold, rate, source)`; the UK plans become example rows |
| Payroll fields (4) | `tax_code`, `ni_category` | A list of `(scheme, code)` pairs per worker, validated against the jurisdiction's scheme list; the two names become `scheme` values. **WPM-D115 generalizes:** no bank detail and **no national identifier of any country** gets a column |
| Public holidays (6) | `holidays.region` | Unchanged; adds `holidays.weekend_days` and week start per code |
| Equality categories (13) | A configured category list | `union` parameter per code; the pay-gap "sex" category stays a named setting |
| Money | Currency per row | Unchanged; the minor-unit exponent comes from the currency (T369 checks the code) |

### What does not change

- **WPM stores parameters, not law** (scope: no labour-law engine). A profile is a deployer's statement with a source, not WPM's claim.
- **Roll-ups, floors and masks are unchanged.** A profile never makes a figure about a person visible; a count under the floor is hidden in
  every jurisdiction.
- **No profile is the default.** The demo seed ships an `example` UK profile **and** a differently shaped example (proposed: one with a
  Sunday-start week, a six-day working week, a different currency exponent and a federal layer) so that nothing in the demo reads as
  "the" shape.

### Order of work

1. A pure `rules::jurisdiction` (registry, chain, `resolve`), with two-profile tests (T369).
2. The tables (`jurisdictions`, `jurisdiction_parameters`), HR-only read and write, audited without figures about people.
3. Move one rule at a time, working time first (it has constants and a clear test), then retention, then pay transparency, then deductions
   and payroll fields.
4. A screen showing, for an organization, each parameter, its value, its source and layer, and its status.

### Needs the product owner

1. **Behaviour change.** **Answered 2026-10-29: yes.** With no profile configured, today's UK/EU working-time flags would become `no limit configured`. Is that right
   for the demo, or does the demo seed always load an example profile (the proposal)?
2. **Who edits a profile.** **Answered 2026-10-29: yes (HR).** HR of the organization (proposed), the deployer only, or both with a review?
3. **Subnational and bloc codes.** **Answered 2026-10-29: yes.** Is ISO 3166 plus a deployer-extended supranational list acceptable, or is a different registry wanted?
4. **Where the work is done.** **Answered 2026-10-29: yes.** Is a new structured `work_jurisdiction` on the worker, set by HR, the right test, and is it HR's to set for a remote worker?
5. **Naming the example profiles.** **Answered 2026-10-29: India first, then Japan** (the UAE as a possible third).

### The parameter registry (WPM-T407, 2026-10-31)

`rules::jurisdiction::REGISTRY` in the service is the registry; this table is its copy and a change to one is a change to both. A
key outside it is refused.

| Key | Shape and unit | Combination |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `calendar.week_start` | one ISO weekday, 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday) | `most_specific` |
| `holidays.weekend_days` | a set of ISO weekdays, at most six; empty means no weekly rest day | `most_specific` |
| `working_time.max_average_weekly_minutes` | whole minutes, 1 to 10,080 | `strictest_max` (the lowest) |
| `working_time.min_daily_rest_minutes` | whole minutes, 1 to 1,440 | `strictest_min` (the highest) |
| `working_time.reference_weeks` | whole weeks of seven calendar days, 1 to 52 | `strictest_max` (the shortest) |

Entries for retention, pay transparency and the other `WPM_*` settings are added as each rule moves (D144's order of work, step 3).
The `union` and `bounded` rules are built and unit-tested with test-only entries; no shipped entry uses them yet.

### What the registry chose (WPM-T407)

The design left these details open; the pure core chose as follows, minimally, and each is a test in `rules::jurisdiction`.

- **Which name is which.** `strictest_max` applies to a maximum (a ceiling, a window, a deadline) and takes the **lowest** value of all
  layers; `strictest_min` applies to a minimum (a rest floor) and takes the **highest**. The reference window is a maximum: a shorter
  window averages over fewer weeks, which protects more. Each parameter combines on its own, so a ceiling and a window may come from
  different layers; the answer names both origins.
- **A tie** between layers keeps the more specific layer as the origin.
- **Dates.** `effective_to` is the last day in force (inclusive). Of a code's rows for a key, the one in force on the date is the one
  with the latest `effective_from` not after it; two rows with the same `effective_from` resolve to the later-recorded one.
- **The chain.** It starts at the work jurisdiction and follows the parents the organization recorded. A code the organization has not
  recorded is a chain of itself alone, at the layer its shape implies (with a subdivision part, subnational; otherwise national); its
  parent is **not** guessed from its prefix, and a supranational layer is never inferred. A parent narrower than its child, a cycle, a
  malformed code or more than eight links is refused. A code with a subdivision part is only subnational; one without is national or
  supranational. The chain is the organization's current one: it is not dated (a past decision is explained by the rows in force that
  day, over today's chain).
- **The answer's status** is the least-checked of the rows that gave it (`example` below `unverified` below `read`), so a value is
  `read` only when every row behind it was read.
- **Unknown has two reasons:** `no_work_jurisdiction` (the place of work is not recorded) and `not_configured` (no row applies; for a
  limit, "no limit configured"). A bounded parameter whose floors and ceilings do not meet is a `conflict` that names the clashing rows.
- **A stored row that no longer fits the registry** (a range tightened later) is skipped as if absent, not trusted.

# ভূমিকাভিত্তিক নথি

প্রতিটি নেতৃত্ব-ভূমিকার জন্য একটি করে পৃষ্ঠা, যা বলে ওয়ার্কফোর্স প্ল্যানিং ম্যানেজমেন্ট (WPM) সেই ভূমিকাকে কী দেয়, এটি যা দেখায় তা কীভাবে পড়তে হয়, এটি কী করবে না এবং কী এখনও খোলা। প্রতিটি পৃষ্ঠা [বিনির্দেশ](../../../spec/index.md)-এর সঙ্গে সংযুক্ত, তা পুনরাবৃত্তি করে না।

| ভূমিকা | পৃষ্ঠা |
| --- | --- |
| প্রধান নির্বাহী কর্মকর্তা (CEO) | [প্রধান-নির্বাহী-কর্মকর্তা](প্রধান-নির্বাহী-কর্মকর্তা/index.md) |
| প্রধান পরিচালন কর্মকর্তা (COO) | [প্রধান-পরিচালন-কর্মকর্তা](প্রধান-পরিচালন-কর্মকর্তা/index.md) |
| প্রধান প্রযুক্তি কর্মকর্তা (CTO) | [প্রধান-প্রযুক্তি-কর্মকর্তা](প্রধান-প্রযুক্তি-কর্মকর্তা/index.md) |
| প্রধান তথ্য কর্মকর্তা (CIO) | [প্রধান-তথ্য-কর্মকর্তা](প্রধান-তথ্য-কর্মকর্তা/index.md) |
| প্রধান ঝুঁকি কর্মকর্তা (CRO) | [প্রধান-ঝুঁকি-কর্মকর্তা](প্রধান-ঝুঁকি-কর্মকর্তা/index.md) |
| প্রধান আইন কর্মকর্তা (CLO) | [প্রধান-আইন-কর্মকর্তা](প্রধান-আইন-কর্মকর্তা/index.md) |
| প্রধান জনবল কর্মকর্তা (CPO) | [প্রধান-জনবল-কর্মকর্তা](প্রধান-জনবল-কর্মকর্তা/index.md) |
| প্রধান কৌশল কর্মকর্তা | [প্রধান-কৌশল-কর্মকর্তা](প্রধান-কৌশল-কর্মকর্তা/index.md) |
| প্রধান নিরাপত্তা কর্মকর্তা | [প্রধান-নিরাপত্তা-কর্মকর্তা](প্রধান-নিরাপত্তা-কর্মকর্তা/index.md) |
| শাসন, ঝুঁকি, সম্মতি | [শাসন-ঝুঁকি-সম্মতি](শাসন-ঝুঁকি-সম্মতি/index.md) |
| স্বাধীন নিরাপত্তা পরীক্ষণ (এটি কমিশন করার সংক্ষিপ্ত বিবরণ) | [স্বাধীন-নিরাপত্তা-পরীক্ষণ](স্বাধীন-নিরাপত্তা-পরীক্ষণ/index.md) |

শুরু করুন [প্রস্তুতি মূল্যায়ন](../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) দিয়ে: রায় হলো এটি ডেমো সফটওয়্যার এবং উচ্চ-নিশ্চয়তার প্রতিষ্ঠানে উৎপাদনে ব্যবহারের জন্য প্রস্তুত নয়।

> এই অনুবাদ একটি AI লিখেছে এবং কোনো মাতৃভাষী এটি পর্যালোচনা করেননি। ইংরেজি সংস্করণের (`locales/en-gb-oxendict/for/`) সঙ্গে পার্থক্য থাকলে ইংরেজি সংস্করণই প্রযোজ্য।

# Dogfennau ar gyfer rolau

Un dudalen ar gyfer pob rôl arwain, sy'n dweud beth mae Workforce Planning Management (WPM) yn ei roi i'r rôl honno, sut i ddarllen yr hyn a ddangosir, beth na fydd yn ei wneud, a beth sydd heb ei gwblhau eto. Mae pob tudalen yn cysylltu â'r [fanyleb](../../../spec/index.md) yn hytrach na'i hailadrodd.

| Rôl | Tudalen |
| --- | --- |
| Prif Swyddog Gweithredol | [prif-swyddog-gweithredol](prif-swyddog-gweithredol/index.md) |
| Prif Swyddog Gweithrediadau | [prif-swyddog-gweithrediadau](prif-swyddog-gweithrediadau/index.md) |
| Prif Swyddog Technoleg | [prif-swyddog-technoleg](prif-swyddog-technoleg/index.md) |
| Prif Swyddog Gwybodaeth | [prif-swyddog-gwybodaeth](prif-swyddog-gwybodaeth/index.md) |
| Prif Swyddog Risg | [prif-swyddog-risg](prif-swyddog-risg/index.md) |
| Prif Swyddog Cyfreithiol | [prif-swyddog-cyfreithiol](prif-swyddog-cyfreithiol/index.md) |
| Prif Swyddog Pobl | [prif-swyddog-pobl](prif-swyddog-pobl/index.md) |
| Prif Swyddog Strategaeth | [prif-swyddog-strategaeth](prif-swyddog-strategaeth/index.md) |
| Prif Swyddog Diogelwch | [prif-swyddog-diogelwch](prif-swyddog-diogelwch/index.md) |
| Llywodraethu, Risg, Cydymffurfio | [llywodraethu-risg-cydymffurfio](llywodraethu-risg-cydymffurfio/index.md) |
| Profi diogelwch annibynnol (briff ar gyfer ei gomisiynu) | [profi-diogelwch-annibynnol](profi-diogelwch-annibynnol/index.md) |

Dechreuwch gyda'r [asesiad parodrwydd](../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md): y dyfarniad yw mai meddalwedd arddangos yw hwn ac nad yw'n barod i'w ddefnyddio'n gynhyrchiol mewn sefydliad sydd angen sicrwydd uchel.

> Ysgrifennwyd y cyfieithiad hwn gan AI ac nid yw siaradwr brodorol wedi'i adolygu. Os yw'n wahanol i'r fersiwn Saesneg (`locales/en-gb-oxendict/for/`), y fersiwn Saesneg sy'n gywir.

# Dokumentation für Rollen

Eine Seite für jede Führungsrolle: Sie sagt, was Workforce Planning Management (WPM) dieser Rolle bietet, wie das Gezeigte zu lesen ist, was es nicht leisten wird und was noch offen ist. Jede Seite verweist auf die [Spezifikation](../../../spec/index.md), statt sie zu wiederholen.

| Rolle | Seite |
| --- | --- |
| Geschäftsführung (CEO) | [geschäftsführung](geschäftsführung/index.md) |
| Betriebsleitung (COO) | [betriebsleitung](betriebsleitung/index.md) |
| Technikleitung (CTO) | [technikleitung](technikleitung/index.md) |
| Informationsleitung (CIO) | [informationsleitung](informationsleitung/index.md) |
| Risikoleitung (CRO) | [risikoleitung](risikoleitung/index.md) |
| Rechtsleitung (CLO) | [rechtsleitung](rechtsleitung/index.md) |
| Personalleitung (CPO) | [personalleitung](personalleitung/index.md) |
| Strategieleitung | [strategieleitung](strategieleitung/index.md) |
| Sicherheitsleitung | [sicherheitsleitung](sicherheitsleitung/index.md) |
| Governance, Risiko, Compliance | [governance-risiko-compliance](governance-risiko-compliance/index.md) |
| Unabhängige Sicherheitsprüfung (ein Briefing zur Beauftragung) | [unabhängige-sicherheitsprüfung](unabhängige-sicherheitsprüfung/index.md) |

Beginnen Sie mit der [Reifegradbewertung](../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md): Das Ergebnis lautet, dass dies Demonstrationssoftware ist und für den Produktivbetrieb in einer Organisation mit hohem Sicherheitsanspruch nicht bereit ist.

> Diese Übersetzung wurde von einer KI verfasst und von keiner Muttersprachlerin und keinem Muttersprachler geprüft. Bei Abweichungen gilt die englische Fassung (`locales/en-gb-oxendict/for/`).

# Documentation for chief roles

One page for each leadership role, saying what Workforce Planning Management gives that role, how to read what it
shows, what it will not do, and what is still open. Each page links into the [specification](../../../spec/index.md)
rather than restating it.

| Role | Page |
| --- | --- |
| Chief Executive Officer | [chief-executive-officer](chief-executive-officer/index.md) |
| Chief Operating Officer | [chief-operating-officer](chief-operating-officer/index.md) |
| Chief Technology Officer | [chief-technology-officer](chief-technology-officer/index.md) |
| Chief Information Officer | [chief-information-officer](chief-information-officer/index.md) |
| Chief Risk Officer | [chief-risk-officer](chief-risk-officer/index.md) |
| Chief Legal Officer | [chief-legal-officer](chief-legal-officer/index.md) |
| Chief People Officer | [chief-people-officer](chief-people-officer/index.md) |
| Chief Strategy Officer | [chief-strategy-officer](chief-strategy-officer/index.md) |
| Chief Security Officer | [chief-security-officer](chief-security-officer/index.md) |
| Governance, Risk, Compliance | [governance-risk-compliance](governance-risk-compliance/index.md) |
| Independent security testing (a brief for commissioning it) | [independent-security-tester](independent-security-tester/index.md) |

Start with the [readiness assessment](../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md): the verdict is that this is
demonstration software and not ready for production use in a high-assurance organization.

# Documentación para cada rol

Una página para cada rol directivo, que dice qué ofrece Workforce Planning Management (WPM) a ese rol, cómo leer lo que muestra, qué no hará y qué sigue abierto. Cada página enlaza con la [especificación](../../../spec/index.md) en lugar de repetirla.

| Rol | Página |
| --- | --- |
| Dirección general (CEO) | [dirección-general](dirección-general/index.md) |
| Dirección de operaciones (COO) | [dirección-de-operaciones](dirección-de-operaciones/index.md) |
| Dirección de tecnología (CTO) | [dirección-de-tecnología](dirección-de-tecnología/index.md) |
| Dirección de sistemas de información (CIO) | [dirección-de-sistemas-de-información](dirección-de-sistemas-de-información/index.md) |
| Dirección de riesgos (CRO) | [dirección-de-riesgos](dirección-de-riesgos/index.md) |
| Dirección jurídica (CLO) | [dirección-jurídica](dirección-jurídica/index.md) |
| Dirección de personas (CPO) | [dirección-de-personas](dirección-de-personas/index.md) |
| Dirección de estrategia | [dirección-de-estrategia](dirección-de-estrategia/index.md) |
| Dirección de seguridad | [dirección-de-seguridad](dirección-de-seguridad/index.md) |
| Gobernanza, riesgo y cumplimiento | [gobernanza-riesgo-cumplimiento](gobernanza-riesgo-cumplimiento/index.md) |
| Pruebas de seguridad independientes (un informe para encargarlas) | [pruebas-de-seguridad-independientes](pruebas-de-seguridad-independientes/index.md) |

Empiece por la [evaluación de preparación](../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md): la conclusión es que este es software de demostración y no está listo para uso en producción en una organización de alta garantía.

> Esta traducción la ha escrito una IA y ningún hablante nativo la ha revisado. Si difiere de la versión en inglés (`locales/en-gb-oxendict/for/`), prevalece la versión en inglés.

# اختبار الأمن المستقل

**السؤال الذي ربما تطرحه:** كيف نجعل أشخاصًا لم يكتبوا هذا البرنامج يهاجمونه، وإلى ماذا نوجّههم، وماذا نفعل بما يجدونه؟

لم يُجرَ أي اختبار مستقل. كتب [نموذج التهديدات](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) المساعد نفسه الذي كتب البرنامج ولم يراجعه أحد غيره، وجرّب المؤلف نفسه كل ضابط يسمّيه. ويسرد [تقييم الجاهزية](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) اختبار الاختراق المستقل بوصفه بوابة لا يغلقها إلا البشر (WPM-T201، **لم يُنجَز**). هذه الصفحة موجز لمن يكلّف بإجراء اختبار. وليست خطة اختبار من مختبِر ولا تحلّ محلها.

## ما الذي يُعطى للمختبِرين

| البند | أين هو | ملاحظات |
| --- | --- | --- |
| نشر يُهاجَم | نشركم أنتم: [دليل النشر](../../../../spec/operations/deployment.md) | إعدادات الإنتاج مع تسجيل الدخول **مفعَّلًا**، ومزوّد هوية للاختبار، و**بيانات اصطناعية فقط**. لا تختبروا على سجلات أشخاص حقيقيين |
| المصدر | هذا المستودع | الاختبار مع المصدر أشمل من الصندوق الأسود؛ حدّدوا أيهما تريدون |
| نموذج التهديدات | [governance/threat-model.md](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) | أربعة وعشرون تهديدًا، والضابط كما بُني، والفجوات. أعطوهم إياه **بعد** جولة الصندوق الأسود الأولى إن أردتم رؤية ما يجدونه دون تلميح |
| وصف واجهة API | `GET /api-docs/openapi.json` | كل مسار، مع `Idempotency-Key` على كل عملية تغيّر شيئًا |
| تصميم تسجيل الدخول | [auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md)، [operations/entra-sign-in.md](../../../../spec/operations/entra-sign-in.md) | الشخصيات والسمات، وأن السياسة تقرّر حسب الإجراء فقط |
| هويات الاختبار | أنتم تنشئونها | على الأقل: عامل بلا سمات، ومدير مباشر، ومدير خارج السلسلة، والموارد البشرية، والرواتب، ومدير نظام، ونظير خدمة |

## ما الذي يُطلب منهم فحصه

لم يتمكن المؤلف من فحص هذه. يسمّي كل صف مدخل نموذج التهديدات نفسه ليمكن تتبّع أي نتيجة.

| المجال | ما يُجرَّب | التهديد |
| --- | --- | --- |
| الرموز | الخلط بين الخوارزميات؛ مجموعة مفاتيح تدور أثناء وجود طلبات جارية؛ رمز منتهٍ أو لم يصبح صالحًا بعد؛ رمز لجمهور آخر | T1، T2 |
| الحاجة إلى المعرفة | كل مسار قراءة بصفة مُستدعٍ بلا سمات وبصفة جار؛ مسار لا يعرفه جدول التصنيف؛ كتابة تسمح بها السياسة ويجب أن يرفضها المعالج | T3، T4، T6 |
| السمات المميّزة | هل يمكن إضافة سمة في رمز أو إعادة تشغيلها أو توريثها؛ من يستطيع إصدارها؛ مدير نظام مشترك أو طويل العمر | T24 |
| الحقن | اختبار عشوائي لكل معامل وجزء مسار وحقل في الجسم؛ تُبنى عبارات المحو والاحتفاظ من معرّفات مضبوطة النوع وقد قُرئت ولم تُختبر عشوائيًا | T12 |
| عميل المتصفح | تعامل خادم الواجهة مع الجلسات، وكيف يبدّل جلسة برمز، والبرمجة النصية عبر المواقع من نص مخزَّن، وتجاوز سياسة أمان المحتوى، وصفحة مدير المحتوى التي تحمّل نصًا برمجيًا من شبكة عامة دون إصدار مثبَّت | T13، T14 |
| الطلبات الصادرة | تزوير الطلبات من جهة الخادم عبر أي عنوان URL مضبوط (مجموعات المفاتيح، والخدمات الشقيقة، والتخزين المؤقت المشترك) | T15 |
| الحدود | حد الجسم، ومهلة الطلب، وحدود المعدل لكل نسخة، والعروض التي تحمّل سجلات مؤسسة كاملة إلى الذاكرة | T16، T17 |
| السجلات | هل تصل بيانات شخصية أو رمز أو سلسلة استعلام إلى سجل | T19 |
| مفاتيح عدم التكرار | مفتاح يستخدمه مُستدعيان؛ المفتاح نفسه مع جسم أو مسار أو استعلام مغيَّر؛ مفتاح يكاد يكون صالحًا؛ جسم كبير جدًا؛ طلبان يتسابقان تحت مفتاح واحد (الاستحواذ مُستدلّ عليه ولم يُختبر في سباق)؛ هل يستطيع غير مُستدعيه قراءة استجابة مخزَّنة | جديد |
| سجل التدقيق | أي طريقة لتغيير مدخل أو إزالته أو تخطّيه؛ نقطة التحقق من السلسلة | T7 |
| النسخ الاحتياطية | الاستعادة من نسخة عُبث بها أو بمفتاح خاطئ؛ هل يعود شخص مُحي | T10، T11 |
| سلسلة التوريد | تثبيت إجراءات البناء، وفحص الأسرار، وتوقيع الصور | T20، T21 |

## قواعد تُحسم قبل أن يبدؤوا

املؤوها مع فريقي الأمن والشؤون القانونية لديكم. لا شيء منها يُحسم هنا.

- **الصلاحية:** من يوقّع أن الاختبار مصرَّح به، ولأي أنظمة وعناوين.
- **النافذة:** التواريخ والساعات، محسوبة بالأيام التقويمية، ومن يُتصل به لإيقافه.
- **النطاق:** ما هو داخل (واجهة API، والواجهة، ومسار تسجيل الدخول، ونص النسخ الاحتياطي) وما هو خارج (خدمة مزوّد الهوية نفسها، وشبكتكم، وكل ما يُشارَك مع أنظمة أخرى).
- **البيانات:** اصطناعية فقط. إذا وجد مختبِر بيانات شخصية حقيقية فمن يُبلَّغ وكيف تُعالَج.
- **الاختبارات المدمّرة:** هل يُسمح بحجب الخدمة والكتابة الجماعية والمحو، وأين.
- **التقارير:** الصيغة، ومقياس الخطورة، ومن يستلم، ومدة الاحتفاظ المسموح بها، وكيف تُعالَج الأسرار التي يعثرون عليها.
- **إعادة الاختبار:** أن يتضمن العقد التحقق من الإصلاحات.

## ما يُفعل بالنتائج

1. سجّلوا كلًّا منها مهمةً في [tasks.md](../../../../spec/tasks.md) مع مرجع المختبِر والدليل والخطورة التي حدّدها. وتبقى النتيجة المعترَض عليها مسجّلة بوصفها معترَضًا عليها مع السبب.
2. أصلحوا باختبار يفشل أولًا. وإذا كان الإصلاح قاعدة فأضيفوها إلى عمود الفجوات في نموذج التهديدات ولا تغلقوها هناك إلا عند نجاح إعادة الاختبار.
3. لا تعلّموا WPM-T201 منجزة حتى يكون التقرير بين أيديكم ولكل نتيجة مالك وتكتمل إعادة الاختبار. حدّثوا [تقييم الجاهزية](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) وقائمة البوابات (WPM-T203) في التغيير نفسه.
4. أبقوا التقرير خارج المستودع إن كان يحوي ما يمكن استغلاله؛ واربطوا بمكان حفظه.

## ما يعنيه التقرير النظيف وما لا يعنيه

الاختبار بلا نتائج يبيّن فقط أن هؤلاء المختبِرين، في هذه النافذة، بهذا النطاق وهذه الهويات، لم يجدوا شيئًا. وهو لا يبيّن غياب العيوب، ولا يشمل إعدادًا غيّرتموه بعد ذلك، ولا يحلّ محل البوابات الأخرى: تدقيق إمكانية الوصول، وتقييم أثر حماية البيانات لديكم موقَّعًا من مسؤولكم، وتمرين استعادة على منصتكم.

## ما لا تفعله هذه الصفحة

لا تسمّي مورّدًا ولا تحدّد سعرًا ولا تعد بمعيار. أيّ مخطط أو اعتماد يتوقعه قطاعكم من المختبِر فهو قراركم.

## مدى حداثة هذه الصفحة

كُتبت في 2026-10-11 استنادًا إلى المواصفات، لا بتشغيل البرنامج من أجل هذه الصفحة. الأرقام التي تتغير (الاختبارات، والترحيلات، والمهام المنجزة) لم تُنسخ هنا؛ اقرأها في [implementation-status.md](../../../../spec/implementation-status.md) الذي يولّده نص برمجي. WPM برنامج للعرض التوضيحي ببيانات اصطناعية: تبيّن هذه الصفحة ما يفعله وما لا يفعله، ولا تدّعي أنه مناسب لمؤسستك. لا شيء هنا يُعدّ استشارة قانونية.

> كتب الذكاءُ الاصطناعي هذه الترجمة ولم يراجعها ناطق أصلي. وإذا اختلفت عن النسخة الإنجليزية (`locales/en-gb-oxendict/for/`) فالنسخة الإنجليزية هي المعتمدة.

# الحوكمة والمخاطر والامتثال

**الأسئلة التي ربما تطرحها:** من المسؤول عن ماذا، وما الذي قد يسوء وما الذي يمنعه، وما الأدلة التي أستطيع أن أعرضها على مقيِّم؟ تجمع هذه الصفحة مواد الحوكمة والمخاطر والامتثال في مكان واحد. وتغطي صفحتا [رئيس المخاطر](../رئيس-المخاطر/index.md) و[رئيس الشؤون القانونية](../رئيس-الشؤون-القانونية/index.md) المجال نفسه حسب الدور.

## الحوكمة: من يقرّر، وكيف يُسجَّل

| الموضوع | ما هو موجود | اقرأ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| كيف يُدار العمل | المواصفات أولًا: يصل المتطلب والقرار والمهمة والشيفرة والاختبارات معًا؛ وكل مهمة تذكر ما **لم** يُتحقَّق منه | [spec-driven-delivery](../../../../AGENTS/spec-driven-delivery.md) |
| حوكمة المشروع | الحوكمة، والمشرفون، وعملية RFC، وملف مالكي الشيفرة | [GOVERNANCE.md](../../../../GOVERNANCE.md)، [RFC.md](../../../../RFC.md)، [MAINTAINERS.md](../../../../MAINTAINERS.md) |
| القرارات المتعلقة بالأشخاص | يقرّر شخص؛ والدرجات تُشير. وتُسجَّل عمليات التحويل والاستقالات وطلبات العمل المرن بوصفها قرار شخص | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md)، [self-service-and-worker-requests.md](../../../../spec/self-service-and-worker-requests.md) |
| الوصول والأدوار | تقرّر الأدوار والسمات الوصول؛ ويقرّر جدول مصنَّف الحاجة إلى المعرفة على كل مسار قراءة | [auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md) |
| التأليف بمساعدة الذكاء الاصطناعي | بيان عن كيفية استخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي | [AI_STATEMENT.md](../../../../AI_STATEMENT.md) |

## المخاطر: ما الذي قد يسوء

| الموضوع | ما هو موجود | اقرأ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| الحكم | **غير جاهز** لنشر عالي الضمان؛ وُجد عائق واحد بالفحص (لم تكن القراءات تتبع الحاجة إلى المعرفة) وأُصلح | [readiness-assessment.md](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) |
| التهديدات | نموذج تهديدات: الأصول، والجهات الفاعلة، والحدود، والضابط كما بُني، وما **لم يُقيَّم** | [governance/threat-model.md](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) |
| دليل العبث | سجل تدقيق للإلحاق فقط، مترابط بالبصمات، مع نقطة تحقق؛ ولا تحتوي مدخلاته نص سبب أو قيمة | [audit.md](../../../../spec/audit.md) |
| إقلاع يفشل بأمان | يرفض الإنتاج الإقلاع مع تعطيل تسجيل الدخول، أو دون مفاتيح رموز، أو باتصال قاعدة بيانات غير مشفّر بمضيف آخر، أو بـRedis بعيد غير مشفّر | [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md) |
| الاستعادة | نسخ احتياطية مشفّرة، وتمرين استعادة يُشغَّل في CI، ودفتر للمحو حتى لا تعيد الاستعادة شخصًا مُحي | [operations/backup-and-restore.md](../../../../spec/operations/backup-and-restore.md) |
| الحوادث | دليل تشغيل بالإجراءات الأولى؛ ويضيف المُنشِر جهات الاتصال ومسارات التصعيد | [operations/runbook.md](../../../../spec/operations/runbook.md) |
| التحيّز في الدرجات | قالب أثر المساواة وسجل لكل درجة، ولكلٍّ منها مسودة تقييم | [equality-impact/register.md](../../../../spec/equality-impact/register.md) |
| المخاطر المفتوحة | تثبيت سلسلة التوريد وتوقيعها، وأدلة الحمل، وفحوص السجلات بحثًا عن بيانات شخصية، وحدود المعدل المشتركة، ومجموعة أدوار قاعدة بيانات بأقل الصلاحيات، وإرشادات إبطال الرموز | [readiness-assessment.md](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md)، القسم 3 |

## الامتثال: ما تستطيع عرضه على مقيِّم

| الموضوع | ما هو موجود | اقرأ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| تقييم ذاتي للضوابط | قائمة تحقق كل إجابة فيها: مستوفاة، أو مستوفاة جزئيًا، أو غير مستوفاة، أو يجيب عنها المُنشِر | [governance/assessment-checklist.md](../../../../spec/governance/assessment-checklist.md) |
| تقييم أثر حماية البيانات | قالب مستكمل للعرض التوضيحي، مع تعليم الأجزاء التي يجب أن تستكملوها | [governance/dpia.md](../../../../spec/governance/dpia.md) |
| سجل المعالجة | سجل قابل للتكييف | [governance/record-of-processing.md](../../../../spec/governance/record-of-processing.md) |
| تدفق البيانات | إلى أين تنتقل البيانات الشخصية | [governance/data-flow.md](../../../../spec/governance/data-flow.md) |
| الاحتفاظ | جدول لكل نوع سجل | [governance/retention-schedule.md](../../../../spec/governance/retention-schedule.md) |
| حقوق أصحاب البيانات | تصدير الوصول والمحو | [regulatory.md](../../../../spec/regulatory.md) |
| بيانات الفئات الخاصة | مراقبة المساواة ومتطلبات الصحة في مكان العمل معطّلتان إلى أن يُسجَّل أساس قانوني، ثم محدودتان | [self-service-and-worker-requests.md](../../../../spec/self-service-and-worker-requests.md) |
| إمكانية الوصول واللغة | بيان إمكانية الوصول وبيان اللغة الرسمية | [governance/accessibility-statement.md](../../../../spec/governance/accessibility-statement.md)، [governance/official-language-statement.md](../../../../spec/governance/official-language-statement.md) |
| التراخيص والتبعيات | ملفات التراخيص، وسياسة تبعيات يفحصها `cargo deny`، وقائمة مكوّنات البرمجيات عند كل إصدار | [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md) |

## ما لا يستطيعه إلا البشر

هذه بوابات لا شيفرة، ولا يعلّمها المستودع منجزة: اختبار اختراق مستقل، وتدقيق مستقل لإمكانية الوصول، وتقييم أثر حماية البيانات لديكم موقَّعًا من مسؤولكم، وتمرين استعادة على منصتكم، ومراجعة مهنية للترجمات، وموافقتكم على تقييمات أثر المساواة.

## حدود هذه الصفحة

تشير الجداول إلى وثائق. وأنتم ومقيِّمكم من يحكم هل كل وثيقة صحيحة بشأن نشركم. واختبارات المؤلف ليست مراجعة مستقلة، ولا شيء هنا استشارة قانونية أو شهادة اعتماد.

## مدى حداثة هذه الصفحة

كُتبت في 2026-10-11 استنادًا إلى المواصفات، لا بتشغيل البرنامج من أجل هذه الصفحة. الأرقام التي تتغير (الاختبارات، والترحيلات، والمهام المنجزة) لم تُنسخ هنا؛ اقرأها في [implementation-status.md](../../../../spec/implementation-status.md) الذي يولّده نص برمجي. WPM برنامج للعرض التوضيحي ببيانات اصطناعية: تبيّن هذه الصفحة ما يفعله وما لا يفعله، ولا تدّعي أنه مناسب لمؤسستك. لا شيء هنا يُعدّ استشارة قانونية.

> كتب الذكاءُ الاصطناعي هذه الترجمة ولم يراجعها ناطق أصلي. وإذا اختلفت عن النسخة الإنجليزية (`locales/en-gb-oxendict/for/`) فالنسخة الإنجليزية هي المعتمدة.

# إلى الرئيس التنفيذي (CEO)

**السؤال الذي ربما تطرحه:** ما حال قوتنا العاملة، وما الذي يحتاج إلى انتباهي، وهل نستطيع الوفاء بما وعدنا به بالأشخاص الذين لدينا؟

## ما الذي تحصل عليه

| ما تريد معرفته | أين يجيب WPM | اقرأ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| حال القوة العاملة في شاشة واحدة | لوحة الرئيس التنفيذي: عدد العاملين وتغيّره، ومعدل الدوران، والشواغر المفتوحة ومدة شغلها، وفجوات التعاقب، واتجاه ستة أشهر، وأبرز الرؤى. بحجم يناسب جهازًا لوحيًا دون تمرير | [communication-and-leadership.md](../../../../spec/communication-and-leadership.md) (WPM-R48) |
| أي الأرقام تستحق الانتباه | رؤى القوة العاملة: استنتاجات مشتقة من الأرقام نفسها، ومع كلٍّ منها ما ينبغي النظر فيه بعد ذلك | WPM-R49، الملف نفسه |
| ما سنحتاج إليه، والفجوة | تخطيط القوة العاملة الاستراتيجي: خطط بوصفها عوالم مسودة، وتوقّع بقواعد شفافة، وفجوات في العدد والكفاءات، ومواءمة مع الأهداف | [strategic-workforce-planning.md](../../../../spec/strategic-workforce-planning.md) |
| هل نستطيع بدء برنامج | قدرة التنفيذ: مجمّعات المهارات، وطلب البرامج، والتزامات الشركاء، وأي مجمّع هو القيد، وفحص البدء | [delivery-capacity.md](../../../../spec/delivery-capacity.md) |
| من يمكنه شغل الأدوار الأساسية | خطط التعاقب وفجوة التعاقب في اللوحة (تحليل مخاطر الأشخاص الأساسيين مخطَّط له ولم يُبنَ بعد) | [talent-development.md](../../../../spec/talent-development.md) |
| كم من الأشخاص غير الدائمين نعتمد عليهم | التعاقدات محددة المدة وتعاقدات المقاولين، وتواريخ انتهائها، والتمويل بجانبها، وخطط التحويل | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md) |

## كيف تُقرأ الأرقام

- الرقم الذي لا يمكن حسابه يظهر مفقودًا، ولا يظهر صفرًا أبدًا. والاتجاه ذو التاريخ القليل جدًا يقول ذلك.
- التوقّع قاعدة مُعلنة مطبّقة على مدخلات مُعلنة، وليس نموذجًا. وكل نتيجة تبيّن ما تستند إليه.
- المجاميع لا تسمّي أحدًا، والمجموعات الصغيرة تُحجب. فلن تحصل من اللوحة على قائمة بأفراد.
- الدرجات تُشير على شخص ولا تقرّر. ولا شيء في WPM يرتّب الأشخاص للفصل أو للأجر.

## ما لن يفعله

- ليس نظامًا مرجعيًا لكشوف الرواتب، وضريبة الرواتب فيه مجرد بديل مؤقت.
- لا يحتفظ ببيانات ديموغرافية. مراقبة المساواة موجودة لكنها **معطّلة** إلى أن يسجّل المُنشِر أساسًا قانونيًا ويحدّد الفئات.
- لم يراجع اللوحةَ شخصٌ يستخدم التقنيات المساعدة.

## قرارات تعود إليك

- هل تنقله إلى ما بعد العرض التوضيحي. [تقييم الجاهزية](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) يقول **غير جاهز** ويسرد البوابات التي لا يغلقها إلا البشر: اختبار اختراق مستقل، وتدقيق لإمكانية الوصول، وتقييم أثر حماية البيانات موقَّعًا من مسؤولكم، وتمرين استعادة على منصتكم.
- أي تقييمات لأثر المساواة تعتمدها قبل استخدام أي درجات ([equality-impact/](../../../../spec/equality-impact/template.md)).

انظر أيضًا صفحات [رئيس العمليات](../رئيس-العمليات/index.md) و[رئيس شؤون الموظفين](../رئيس-شؤون-الموظفين/index.md) و[رئيس المخاطر](../رئيس-المخاطر/index.md).

## مدى حداثة هذه الصفحة

كُتبت في 2026-10-11 استنادًا إلى المواصفات، لا بتشغيل البرنامج من أجل هذه الصفحة. الأرقام التي تتغير (الاختبارات، والترحيلات، والمهام المنجزة) لم تُنسخ هنا؛ اقرأها في [implementation-status.md](../../../../spec/implementation-status.md) الذي يولّده نص برمجي. WPM برنامج للعرض التوضيحي ببيانات اصطناعية: تبيّن هذه الصفحة ما يفعله وما لا يفعله، ولا تدّعي أنه مناسب لمؤسستك. لا شيء هنا يُعدّ استشارة قانونية.

> كتب الذكاءُ الاصطناعي هذه الترجمة ولم يراجعها ناطق أصلي. وإذا اختلفت عن النسخة الإنجليزية (`locales/en-gb-oxendict/for/`) فالنسخة الإنجليزية هي المعتمدة.
