| Retention | A schedule per record kind, with a sweep for some | [governance/retention-schedule.md](../../../../spec/governance/retention-schedule.md) |
| Subject rights | Subject access export, erasure, and an erasure ledger | [regulatory.md](../../../../spec/regulatory.md) (WPM-R30) |
| Special-category data | Equality monitoring and workplace health requirements are off until you record a lawful basis, then bounded: voluntary, self-only or role-limited, aggregates above a floor, never used in a decision | [self-service-and-worker-requests.md](../../../../spec/self-service-and-worker-requests.md) |
| Statutory rights | Flexible working requests with a decision period and reasons you configure; resignation notice you configure | [operations/deployment.md](../../../../spec/operations/deployment.md) |
| Equality duties | An equality impact template and a register of every score | [equality-impact/template.md](../../../../spec/equality-impact/template.md) |
| Accessibility and language | An accessibility statement and an official-language statement | [governance/accessibility-statement.md](../../../../spec/governance/accessibility-statement.md), [governance/official-language-statement.md](../../../../spec/governance/official-language-statement.md) |
| Collective bodies | Research and proposal for recognized bodies and consultation, never individual membership | [worker-unions.md](../../../../spec/worker-unions.md) |
| Contractors | Engagement basis, the supplier, route and masked rate are recorded. Whether an engagement is lawful or correctly classified is not something the software decides | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md) |
| Licences | Licence files, a dependency policy and a software bill of materials on release | [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md) |

## Defaults that are not law

Several settings are defaults, not legal advice: the resignation notice, the flexible working decision period and
appeal period, and the refusal reasons. The deployment guide says to **confirm them** for your jurisdiction.
Statutory calculations such as payroll tax are not implemented.

## Decisions that are yours

Lawful basis for each processing purpose, the data protection impact assessment and its sign-off, processor
agreements, the retention schedule you adopt, and whether to turn on any special-category feature.

# For the Chief Operating Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** do we have the right people, in the right place, at the right time, and
what breaks if someone is away?

## What you get

| You want to know | Where WPM answers | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Can a team cover absence | Backups per person, the on-call rota with swaps and reminders, and a cover view that says plainly when nobody is available | [people-directory-and-cover.md](../../../../spec/people-directory-and-cover.md) |
| Time, attendance and leave | Time entries, leave requests with an approval path, accruals, and shifts | [workforce-management.md](../../../../spec/workforce-management.md) |
| Are working-time limits being respected | Advisory working-time guardrails; they warn and do not block | WPM-R27, same file |
| Capacity by skill, month by month | Skill pools, supply and programme demand, partner commitments, the constraint pool, and a start check that is a suggestion, with recorded start decisions | [delivery-capacity.md](../../../../spec/delivery-capacity.md) |
| What we will need and where the gap is | Workforce plans, forecast and gap analysis by department and by role | [strategic-workforce-planning.md](../../../../spec/strategic-workforce-planning.md) |
| Which contracts end soon | An end date by engagement basis, extensions with history, reminders before an end, a list of engagements missing an end date, and conversion plans | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md) |
| Where contingent staff are a large share | The share of FTE that is contractor and that is fixed-term, each apart, and the funding that ends month by month | `GET /api/workforce-intelligence/contingent` (WPM-T109) |
| Joiners and leavers | Dated checklists, and a last-day handover | [joiners-and-leavers.md](../../../../spec/joiners-and-leavers.md) |
| Skills gaps and training time | Gap analysis with the evidence a recommendation rests on | [skills-and-training.md](../../../../spec/skills-and-training.md) |

## How to read the capacity view

Capacity is planned by skill pool, not by person. A pool-month comes to one of four results, and an undeclared
skill is *unknown*, not a shortfall. The start check is a suggestion, and a person records the decision to start.
Critical chain and critical path scheduling are not here: they belong to project-portfolio-management.

## Limits

- Contingent share has no trend yet: it needs headcount snapshots split by basis (WPM-T139, not built).
- A pool for the contingent view is the department until plans define pools.
- Shift scheduling and payroll tax calculations are not a substitute for your rostering or payroll systems.
- Several views load an organization's records into memory; no load figure has been measured
  ([readiness-assessment.md](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md), gap 8).

See also [Chief People Officer](../chief-people-officer/index.md) and [Chief Executive Officer](../chief-executive-officer/index.md).

# For the Chief People Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** does this support the whole employee lifecycle, and can I use it without
holding more about people than I should?

## What you get

| Stage | What WPM holds | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hiring | Requisitions, an applicant pipeline, a candidate pool, onboarding checklists | [talent-acquisition.md](../../../../spec/talent-acquisition.md) |
| The record | One employment record per worker, the org chart, reporting lines, groups, transfers between organizations | [hr-core.md](../../../../spec/hr-core.md) |
| Self-service | A worker sees and updates their own details, requests flexible working, gives notice, and sees their time off | [self-service-and-worker-requests.md](../../../../spec/self-service-and-worker-requests.md) |
| Working life | Leave, time, shifts, benefits, wellbeing prompts, reasonable adjustments, ergonomic assessments, the anonymous pulse | [hr-core.md](../../../../spec/hr-core.md), [workforce-management.md](../../../../spec/workforce-management.md) |
| Development | Reviews, 360 appraisals, courses through the course registry, assessments, mentorships, development plans, succession, early careers | [talent-development.md](../../../../spec/talent-development.md) |
| Pay | Payroll runs, payslips, salary benchmarking, a national pay scale lookup, job levels | [payroll-compensation.md](../../../../spec/payroll-compensation.md), [pay-scales.md](../../../../spec/pay-scales.md) |
| Non-permanent staff | End dates by basis, extensions, status assessments, conversion plans decided by a person, funding beside the contract end | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md) |
| Leaving | Resignation with a notice period, a last-day handover, retention per record kind, erasure | [joiners-and-leavers.md](../../../../spec/joiners-and-leavers.md) |

## How it protects people

- **Need to know on reads.** A manager sees their own reports, a worker sees themselves, HR sees what HR needs.
  A signed-in stranger sees nothing about a colleague ([auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md)).
- **No diagnosis is stored.** Sick leave records a kind, not a reason.
- **Special-category features are off by default.** Equality monitoring and workplace health requirements need a
  recorded lawful basis, are voluntary or held by the occupational health role, and show only groups above a floor.
  They are never an input to any score or decision about a person.
- **Scores advise.** Succession readiness, skill gaps and forecasts suggest; a person decides, and decisions such
  as converting a contractor are recorded as a person's decision, never an automatic outcome.
- **The subject can see and erase.** Subject access export and erasure cover the records above, with a ledger so
  a restore does not bring an erased person back.

## Limits

- Not yet built: a user interface for conversion plans and funding, the contingent trend, and the worker's
  "my details" page. Check [tasks.md](../../../../spec/tasks.md) for the current state.
- Translations are machine-assisted; a professional review is an open gate.
- Collective agreements and recognized bodies are research and proposal only ([worker-unions.md](../../../../spec/worker-unions.md)).
- Payroll tax is a stub.

See also [Chief Legal Officer](../chief-legal-officer/index.md) and [Chief Executive Officer](../chief-executive-officer/index.md).

# For the Chief Risk Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** what could go wrong with this system, what stops it, and what has nobody
checked?

## The honest starting point

The [readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) of 2026-10-11 gives the verdict **not ready** for a
high-assurance deployment. It found one blocker by probing the running service: any signed-in person could read a
colleague's sick leave and its free-text reason. That is fixed and tested. The gates only people can close are
still open.

## What you get

| Concern | What exists | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Threats at each boundary | A threat model: assets, actors, boundaries, the control as built, and what is **not assessed** | [governance/threat-model.md](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) |
| Unauthorized reads | A need-to-know guard that classifies every read route; a test fails on an unclassified one | [auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md) (WPM-R114) |
| Tampering and accountability | An append-only, hash-chained audit trail with a verify endpoint; entries hold no reason text or value | [audit.md](../../../../spec/audit.md) (WPM-R115) |
| Sensitive data | No diagnosis stored; special-category features off by default; a small-group floor | [regulatory.md](../../../../spec/regulatory.md) |
| Insecure paths | Production refuses to start with sign-in off, no token key source, a plaintext database connection to another host, or a plaintext remote Redis | [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md) |
| Loss of data | Encrypted backups, a restore drill run in CI, an erasure ledger | [operations/backup-and-restore.md](../../../../spec/operations/backup-and-restore.md) |
| Bias in scoring | An equality impact template, and a register of every score with a draft assessment | [equality-impact/register.md](../../../../spec/equality-impact/register.md) |

should we do about the gap?

| Where the gap is | Projected supply against planned demand: a headcount gap and a competency gap, with levers listed as suggestions and their evidence | WPM-R37 |
| Whether it serves the strategy | Objectives linked to demand: unresourced objectives, unaligned demand, critical roles with no bench | WPM-R38 |
| Whether we can deliver a programme | Skill pools, programme demand, partner commitments, the constraint pool, a start check that is a suggestion | [delivery-capacity.md](../../../../spec/delivery-capacity.md) |

# Independent security testing

**The question you are likely asking:** how do we get people who did not write this software to attack it, what should
we point them at, and what do we do with what they find?

No independent test has been done. The [threat model](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) was written by the
same assistant that wrote the software and was reviewed by no one else, and every control it names was exercised by
that author. The [readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) lists an independent penetration test
as a gate only people can close (WPM-T201, **not done**). This page is a brief for whoever commissions one. It is not a
test plan from a tester and it does not replace one.

## What to give the testers

| Item | Where it is | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A deployment to attack | Yours: [deployment guide](../../../../spec/operations/deployment.md) | Production settings with sign-in **on**, a test identity provider, and **synthetic data only**. Do not test against real people's records |
| The source | This repository | A test with the source is more thorough than a black-box one; say which you want |
| The threat model | [governance/threat-model.md](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) | Twenty-four threats, the control as built, and the gaps. Give it to them **after** a first black-box pass if you want to see what they find unprompted |
| The API description | `GET /api-docs/openapi.json` | Every route, with the `Idempotency-Key` on every operation that changes something |
| The sign-in design | [auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md), [operations/entra-sign-in.md](../../../../spec/operations/entra-sign-in.md) | Personas, attributes, and what the policy decides by action only |
| Test identities | You create them | At least: a worker with no attributes, a line manager, a manager outside the chain, HR, payroll, an administrator, and a service peer |

## What to ask them to look at

The author could not check these. Each row names the threat model's own entry, so a finding can be traced.

| Area | What to try | Threat |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tokens | Algorithm confusion, a key set that rotates while requests are in flight, an expired or not-yet-valid token, a token for another audience | T1, T2 |
| Need to know | Every read route as a caller with no attributes and as a neighbour; a route the classification table does not know; a write that the policy allows but the handler should refuse | T3, T4, T6 |
| Privileged attributes | Whether an attribute in a token can be added, replayed or inherited; who can mint one; a shared or long-lived administrator | T24 |
| Injection | Fuzz every parameter, path segment and body field; the erasure and retention statements are built from typed identifiers and were read, not fuzzed | T12 |
| The browser client | Session handling by the interface server, how it exchanges a session for a token, cross-site scripting through stored text, a content security policy bypass, the content manager's page that loads a script from a public network without a pinned version | T13, T14 |
| Outbound requests | Server-side request forgery through any configured URL (key sets, the sibling services, the shared cache) | T15 |
| Limits | The body limit, the request timeout, the rate limits per instance, and the views that load a whole organization's records into memory | T16, T17 |
| Logs | Whether any personal data, token or query string reaches a log | T19 |
| Idempotency keys | A key used by two callers; the same key with a changed body, path or query; a key that is almost valid; a very large body; two requests racing under one key (the claim is reasoned, not raced by a test); whether a stored response can be read by anyone but its caller | new |
| The audit trail | Any way to change, remove or skip an entry; the chain verification endpoint | T7 |
| Backups | Restore from a tampered or wrongly keyed backup; whether an erased person returns | T10, T11 |
| Supply chain | Pinning of build actions, secret scanning, image signing | T20, T21 |

## Rules to settle before they start

Fill these in with your own security and legal teams. None is decided here.

- **Authority:** who signs that the test is authorized, and for which systems and addresses.
- **Window:** the dates and hours, counted in calendar days, and who to call to stop it.
- **Scope:** what is in (the API, the interface, the sign-in flow, the backup script) and what is out (the identity
  provider's own service, your network, anything shared with other systems).
- **Data:** synthetic only. If a tester finds real personal data, who is told and how it is handled.
- **Destructive tests:** whether denial of service, bulk writes and erasure are allowed, and where.
- **Reporting:** the format, the severity scale, who receives it, how long they may keep it, and how secrets they
  find are handled.
- **Retest:** that the contract includes checking the fixes.

## What to do with the findings

1. Record each as a task in [tasks.md](../../../../spec/tasks.md) with the tester's reference, the evidence, and the
   severity they gave. A finding that is disputed stays recorded as disputed, with the reason.
2. Fix with a test that fails first. Where the fix is a rule, add it to the threat model's gap column and close it
   there only when the retest passes.
3. Do not mark WPM-T201 done until the report is in hand, every finding has an owner, and a retest is complete. Update
   the [readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) and the gates list (WPM-T203) in the same change.
4. Keep the report out of the repository if it holds anything exploitable; link to where it is held.

## What a clean report does and does not mean

A test with no findings shows that these testers, in this window, with this scope and these identities, found nothing.
It does not show the absence of flaws, it does not cover a configuration you changed afterwards, and it does not
replace the other gates: an accessibility audit, your data protection impact assessment signed off, and a restore drill on
your platform.

## What this page does not do

It does not name a supplier, set a price or promise a standard. Which scheme or accreditation your sector expects of a
tester is for you to decide.

Sized to fit a tablet without scrolling | [communication-and-leadership.md](../../../../spec/communication-and-leadership.md) (WPM-R48) |
| Which numbers deserve attention | Workforce insights: findings derived from the same figures, each with what to look at next | WPM-R49, same file |

# For the Chief Information Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** how does this fit our estate, who can sign in, where does the data live,
and how do we run and recover it?

| Concern | What exists | Read |

| Deployment | A container build and a compose file for a demonstration; for production a TLS-terminating proxy, required settings, and boot checks that refuse an insecure setup | [operations/deployment.md](../../../../spec/operations/deployment.md) |
| Shared cache | Optional Redis for non-personal lookups only; every call fails open | `REDIS_URL` in the deployment guide (WPM-D78) |

| Upgrade | Migrations and an upgrade guide | [operations/upgrade-and-migration.md](../../../../spec/operations/upgrade-and-migration.md) |
| When it goes wrong | A runbook of first actions | [operations/runbook.md](../../../../spec/operations/runbook.md) |
| Data movement | A data flow document | [governance/data-flow.md](../../../../spec/governance/data-flow.md) |

## Things to know before you plan

- The UI is **not containerised**; you choose an adapter for your platform.
- Rate limits are per instance. A shared store is yours to provide.
- The application uses whatever database role `DATABASE_URL` names; a least-privilege role set is not yet provided.
- Token revocation and maximum token age are your identity provider's.
- Managed Redis (cluster, sentinel, access-control users) has not been tried.
- No load measurement exists, and some views read an organisation into memory.

**The question you are likely asking:** what legal duties does this software create or help with, and what must
we decide before real data goes in?

## What you get

| Topic | What exists | Read |

| Subject rights | Subject access export, erasure, and an erasure ledger | [regulatory.md](../../../../spec/regulatory.md) (WPM-R30) |
| Special-category data | Equality monitoring and workplace health requirements are off until you record a lawful basis, then bounded: voluntary, self-only or role-limited, aggregates above a floor, never used in a decision | [self-service-and-worker-requests.md](../../../../spec/self-service-and-worker-requests.md) |
| Statutory rights | Flexible working requests with a decision period and reasons you configure; resignation notice you configure | [operations/deployment.md](../../../../spec/operations/deployment.md) |
| Equality duties | An equality impact template and a register of every score | [equality-impact/template.md](../../../../spec/equality-impact/template.md) |

| Collective bodies | Research and proposal for recognised bodies and consultation, never individual membership | [worker-unions.md](../../../../spec/worker-unions.md) |
| Contractors | Engagement basis, the supplier, route and masked rate are recorded. Whether an engagement is lawful or correctly classified is not something the software decides | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md) |
| Licences | Licence files, a dependency policy and a software bill of materials on release | [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md) |

## Defaults that are not law

Several settings are defaults, not legal advice: the resignation notice, the flexible working decision period and
appeal period, and the refusal reasons. The deployment guide says to **confirm them** for your jurisdiction.
Statutory calculations such as payroll tax are not implemented.

## Decisions that are yours

Lawful basis for each processing purpose, the data protection impact assessment and its sign-off, processor
agreements, the retention schedule you adopt, and whether to turn on any special-category feature.

# For the Chief Operating Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** do we have the right people, in the right place, at the right time, and
what breaks if someone is away?

## What you get

| You want to know | Where WPM answers | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Can a team cover absence | Backups per person, the on-call rota with swaps and reminders, and a cover view that says plainly when nobody is available | [people-directory-and-cover.md](../../../../spec/people-directory-and-cover.md) |
| Time, attendance and leave | Time entries, leave requests with an approval path, accruals, and shifts | [workforce-management.md](../../../../spec/workforce-management.md) |
| Are working-time limits being respected | Advisory working-time guardrails; they warn and do not block | WPM-R27, same file |
| Capacity by skill, month by month | Skill pools, supply and programme demand, partner commitments, the constraint pool, and a start check that is a suggestion, with recorded start decisions | [delivery-capacity.md](../../../../spec/delivery-capacity.md) |
| What we will need and where the gap is | Workforce plans, forecast and gap analysis by department and by role | [strategic-workforce-planning.md](../../../../spec/strategic-workforce-planning.md) |
| Which contracts end soon | An end date by engagement basis, extensions with history, reminders before an end, a list of engagements missing an end date, and conversion plans | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md) |
| Where contingent staff are a large share | The share of FTE that is contractor and that is fixed-term, each apart, and the funding that ends month by month | `GET /api/workforce-intelligence/contingent` (WPM-T109) |
| Joiners and leavers | Dated checklists, and a last-day handover | [joiners-and-leavers.md](../../../../spec/joiners-and-leavers.md) |
| Skills gaps and training time | Gap analysis with the evidence a recommendation rests on | [skills-and-training.md](../../../../spec/skills-and-training.md) |

## How to read the capacity view

Capacity is planned by skill pool, not by person. A pool-month comes to one of four results, and an undeclared
skill is *unknown*, not a shortfall. The start check is a suggestion, and a person records the decision to start.
Critical chain and critical path scheduling are not here: they belong to project-portfolio-management.

## Limits

- Contingent share has no trend yet: it needs headcount snapshots split by basis (WPM-T139, not built).
- A pool for the contingent view is the department until plans define pools.
- Shift scheduling and payroll tax calculations are not a substitute for your rostering or payroll systems.
- Several views load an organisation's records into memory; no load figure has been measured
  ([readiness-assessment.md](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md), gap 8).

# For the Chief People Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** does this support the whole employee lifecycle, and can I use it without
holding more about people than I should?

## What you get

| Stage | What WPM holds | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hiring | Requisitions, an applicant pipeline, a candidate pool, onboarding checklists | [talent-acquisition.md](../../../../spec/talent-acquisition.md) |
| The record | One employment record per worker, the org chart, reporting lines, groups, transfers between organisations | [hr-core.md](../../../../spec/hr-core.md) |
| Self-service | A worker sees and updates their own details, requests flexible working, gives notice, and sees their time off | [self-service-and-worker-requests.md](../../../../spec/self-service-and-worker-requests.md) |
| Working life | Leave, time, shifts, benefits, wellbeing prompts, reasonable adjustments, ergonomic assessments, the anonymous pulse | [hr-core.md](../../../../spec/hr-core.md), [workforce-management.md](../../../../spec/workforce-management.md) |
| Development | Reviews, 360 appraisals, courses through the course registry, assessments, mentorships, development plans, succession, early careers | [talent-development.md](../../../../spec/talent-development.md) |
| Pay | Payroll runs, payslips, salary benchmarking, a national pay scale lookup, job levels | [payroll-compensation.md](../../../../spec/payroll-compensation.md), [pay-scales.md](../../../../spec/pay-scales.md) |
| Non-permanent staff | End dates by basis, extensions, status assessments, conversion plans decided by a person, funding beside the contract end | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md) |
| Leaving | Resignation with a notice period, a last-day handover, retention per record kind, erasure | [joiners-and-leavers.md](../../../../spec/joiners-and-leavers.md) |

## How it protects people

- **Need to know on reads.** A manager sees their own reports, a worker sees themselves, HR sees what HR needs.
  A signed-in stranger sees nothing about a colleague ([auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md)).
- **No diagnosis is stored.** Sick leave records a kind, not a reason.
- **Special-category features are off by default.** Equality monitoring and workplace health requirements need a
  recorded lawful basis, are voluntary or held by the occupational health role, and show only groups above a floor.
  They are never an input to any score or decision about a person.
- **Scores advise.** Succession readiness, skill gaps and forecasts suggest; a person decides, and decisions such
  as converting a contractor are recorded as a person's decision, never an automatic outcome.
- **The subject can see and erase.** Subject access export and erasure cover the records above, with a ledger so
  a restore does not bring an erased person back.

## Limits

- Not yet built: a user interface for conversion plans and funding, the contingent trend, and the worker's
  "my details" page. Check [tasks.md](../../../../spec/tasks.md) for the current state.
- Translations are machine-assisted; a professional review is an open gate.
- Collective agreements and recognised bodies are research and proposal only ([worker-unions.md](../../../../spec/worker-unions.md)).
- Payroll tax is a stub.

See also [Chief Legal Officer](../chief-legal-officer/index.md) and [Chief Executive Officer](../chief-executive-officer/index.md).

# For the Chief Risk Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** what could go wrong with this system, what stops it, and what has nobody
checked?

## The honest starting point

The [readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) of 2026-10-11 gives the verdict **not ready** for a
high-assurance deployment. It found one blocker by probing the running service: any signed-in person could read a
colleague's sick leave and its free-text reason. That is fixed and tested. The gates only people can close are
still open.

## What you get

| Concern | What exists | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Threats at each boundary | A threat model: assets, actors, boundaries, the control as built, and what is **not assessed** | [governance/threat-model.md](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) |
| Unauthorised reads | A need-to-know guard that classifies every read route; a test fails on an unclassified one | [auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md) (WPM-R114) |
| Tampering and accountability | An append-only, hash-chained audit trail with a verify endpoint; entries hold no reason text or value | [audit.md](../../../../spec/audit.md) (WPM-R115) |
| Sensitive data | No diagnosis stored; special-category features off by default; a small-group floor | [regulatory.md](../../../../spec/regulatory.md) |
| Insecure paths | Production refuses to start with sign-in off, no token key source, a plaintext database connection to another host, or a plaintext remote Redis | [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md) |
| Loss of data | Encrypted backups, a restore drill run in CI, an erasure ledger | [operations/backup-and-restore.md](../../../../spec/operations/backup-and-restore.md) |
| Bias in scoring | An equality impact template, and a register of every score with a draft assessment | [equality-impact/register.md](../../../../spec/equality-impact/register.md) |
| A control self-assessment | A checklist with each answer met, partly met, not met, or for the deployer to answer | [governance/assessment-checklist.md](../../../../spec/governance/assessment-checklist.md) |

## Open risks, as recorded

Supply-chain pinning and signing, load evidence, log checks for personal data, shared rate limits across
instances, a least-privilege database role set, and token revocation guidance are open items in the readiness
assessment, each with a task. The tests were written by the author; none is an independent review.

## What only people can do

An independent penetration test, an independent accessibility audit, the deployer's impact assessment signed off,
a restore drill on your platform, and approval of equality impact assessments. The repository states these
as gates and does not mark them done.

See also [Chief Information Officer](../chief-information-officer/index.md) and [Chief Legal Officer](../chief-legal-officer/index.md).

# For the Chief Security Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** how is this protected, how would we know if it were attacked or misused, and
what has nobody tested?

## What you get

| Concern | What exists | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Threats | A threat model: assets, actors, trust boundaries, the control as built, and what is **not assessed** | [governance/threat-model.md](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) |
| Authentication | Sign-in on by default; production refuses to start with it off or with no token key source; enterprise directory sign-in (OIDC) | [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md), [operations/entra-sign-in.md](../../../../spec/operations/entra-sign-in.md) |
| Authorisation | The policy decides by action only; a classified table decides need to know on every read route, and a source-scan test fails on an unclassified route | [auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md) |
| Audit | An append-only, hash-chained trail with a verify endpoint; entries carry no reason text and no value | [audit.md](../../../../spec/audit.md) |
| Transport and browser | Security headers on every API response, an explicit CORS allow-list that fails boot when unset, `no-store` on `/api` | WPM-R73 in [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md) |
| Abuse | Rate limits per caller, stricter for erase, import, export and token routes | WPM-R74, same file |
| Insecure configuration | Boot refuses a plaintext database connection or plaintext Redis to another host, and a missing CORS origin | [operations/deployment.md](../../../../spec/operations/deployment.md) |
| Data at rest | Encrypted backups; the shared cache holds non-personal lookups only and fails open | [operations/backup-and-restore.md](../../../../spec/operations/backup-and-restore.md) |
| Supply chain | Licence and ban checks with `cargo deny`, version-pinned shared crates, a software bill of materials on release | [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md) |
| Incidents | A runbook of first actions; you add contacts and notification duties | [operations/runbook.md](../../../../spec/operations/runbook.md) |
| Self-assessment | A control checklist: met, partly met, not met, deployer to answer | [governance/assessment-checklist.md](../../../../spec/governance/assessment-checklist.md) |

## Known gaps, as recorded

- No independent penetration test has been done. The tests were written by the author.
- Actions are pinned by tag, not by digest, and images are not signed.
- Rate limits are per instance.
- The application uses whatever database role it is given; no least-privilege role set is provided.
- Token revocation and maximum token age are your identity provider's.
- The content manager's path loads a script from a public CDN without a pinned version or an integrity hash.
- Logs have not been checked for personal data, and the audit trail is not exported to a monitoring system.
- A managed Redis (cluster, sentinel, access-control users) has not been tried.

## What only people can do

Commission the independent penetration test, review the threat model for your environment, run a restore drill on
your platform, and set branch protection on the hosting platform. See the
[readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md), whose verdict is **not ready** for a high-assurance deployment.

See also the [Chief Risk Officer](../chief-risk-officer/index.md) and
[Chief Information Officer](../chief-information-officer/index.md) pages.

# For the Chief Strategy Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** is our workforce shaped to serve the strategy, what will we need, and what
should we do about the gap?

## What you get

| You want to know | Where WPM answers | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What a role requires | Role profiles with required skills and a minimum proficiency, so a gap is measured against a role and not a person | [strategic-workforce-planning.md](../../../../spec/strategic-workforce-planning.md) (WPM-R34) |
| What we will need | Workforce plans as draft worlds, several side by side, with stated assumptions and demand by department, role and period | WPM-R36, same file |
| Where the gap is | Projected supply against planned demand: a headcount gap and a competency gap, with levers listed as suggestions and their evidence | WPM-R37 |
| Whether it serves the strategy | Objectives linked to demand: unresourced objectives, unaligned demand, critical roles with no bench | WPM-R38 |
| Whether we can deliver a programme | Skill pools, programme demand, partner commitments, the constraint pool, a start check that is a suggestion | [delivery-capacity.md](../../../../spec/delivery-capacity.md) |
| How much we rely on non-permanent staff | The share of FTE that is contractor and fixed-term, each apart, and how much funding ends in each of the next twelve months | `GET /api/workforce-intelligence/contingent` (WPM-T109, part) |
| What we plan to do about contracts ending | Conversion plans: a person's decision to convert, extend or end, with the funding beside the contract end | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md) |
| What else is planned | The roadmap and the open task list | [roadmap.md](../../../../spec/roadmap.md), [tasks.md](../../../../spec/tasks.md) |

## How to read a forecast

- It is a stated rule applied to stated inputs, not a model, and every result names its assumptions.
- With too little headcount history it says `insufficient_history` rather than extrapolating.
- A plan holds hypothetical headcount only. It never reads or changes a person's record.
- Levers are suggestions. The planner chooses, and nothing is decided by the software.

## Limits

- The "convert contingent to permanent" lever in plans is specified (WPM-R63) and not yet in code.
- Contingent share has no trend yet: it needs snapshots split by basis (WPM-T139, not built).
- Critical chain and critical path scheduling belong to project-portfolio-management, not here.
- No user interface exists yet for funding or conversion plans.

independent accessibility audit, your data protection impact assessment signed off by your officer, a restore drill
on your platform, a professional review of the translations, and your approval of the equality impact assessments.

## Limits of this page

The tables point at documents. Whether each document is true of your deployment is for you and your assessor.
The author's tests are not an independent review, and nothing here is legal advice or a certification.

# Independent security testing

**The question you are likely asking:** how do we get people who did not write this software to attack it, what should
we point them at, and what do we do with what they find?

No independent test has been done. The [threat model](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) was written by the
same assistant that wrote the software and was reviewed by no one else, and every control it names was exercised by
that author. The [readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) lists an independent penetration test
as a gate only people can close (WPM-T201, **not done**). This page is a brief for whoever commissions one. It is not a
test plan from a tester and it does not replace one.

## What to give the testers

| Item | Where it is | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A deployment to attack | Yours: [deployment guide](../../../../spec/operations/deployment.md) | Production settings with sign-in **on**, a test identity provider, and **synthetic data only**. Do not test against real people's records |
| The source | This repository | A test with the source is more thorough than a black-box one; say which you want |
| The threat model | [governance/threat-model.md](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) | Twenty-four threats, the control as built, and the gaps. Give it to them **after** a first black-box pass if you want to see what they find unprompted |
| The API description | `GET /api-docs/openapi.json` | Every route, with the `Idempotency-Key` on every operation that changes something |
| The sign-in design | [auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md), [operations/entra-sign-in.md](../../../../spec/operations/entra-sign-in.md) | Personas, attributes, and what the policy decides by action only |
| Test identities | You create them | At least: a worker with no attributes, a line manager, a manager outside the chain, HR, payroll, an administrator, and a service peer |

## What to ask them to look at

The author could not check these. Each row names the threat model's own entry, so a finding can be traced.

| Area | What to try | Threat |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tokens | Algorithm confusion, a key set that rotates while requests are in flight, an expired or not-yet-valid token, a token for another audience | T1, T2 |
| Need to know | Every read route as a caller with no attributes and as a neighbour; a route the classification table does not know; a write that the policy allows but the handler should refuse | T3, T4, T6 |
| Privileged attributes | Whether an attribute in a token can be added, replayed or inherited; who can mint one; a shared or long-lived administrator | T24 |
| Injection | Fuzz every parameter, path segment and body field; the erasure and retention statements are built from typed identifiers and were read, not fuzzed | T12 |
| The browser client | Session handling by the interface server, how it exchanges a session for a token, cross-site scripting through stored text, a content security policy bypass, the content manager's page that loads a script from a public network without a pinned version | T13, T14 |
| Outbound requests | Server-side request forgery through any configured URL (key sets, the sibling services, the shared cache) | T15 |
| Limits | The body limit, the request timeout, the rate limits per instance, and the views that load a whole organisation's records into memory | T16, T17 |
| Logs | Whether any personal data, token or query string reaches a log | T19 |
| Idempotency keys | A key used by two callers; the same key with a changed body, path or query; a key that is almost valid; a very large body; two requests racing under one key (the claim is reasoned, not raced by a test); whether a stored response can be read by anyone but its caller | new |
| The audit trail | Any way to change, remove or skip an entry; the chain verification endpoint | T7 |
| Backups | Restore from a tampered or wrongly keyed backup; whether an erased person returns | T10, T11 |
| Supply chain | Pinning of build actions, secret scanning, image signing | T20, T21 |

## Rules to settle before they start

Fill these in with your own security and legal teams. None is decided here.

- **Authority:** who signs that the test is authorised, and for which systems and addresses.
- **Window:** the dates and hours, counted in calendar days, and who to call to stop it.
- **Scope:** what is in (the API, the interface, the sign-in flow, the backup script) and what is out (the identity
  provider's own service, your network, anything shared with other systems).
- **Data:** synthetic only. If a tester finds real personal data, who is told and how it is handled.
- **Destructive tests:** whether denial of service, bulk writes and erasure are allowed, and where.
- **Reporting:** the format, the severity scale, who receives it, how long they may keep it, and how secrets they
  find are handled.
- **Retest:** that the contract includes checking the fixes.

## What to do with the findings

1. Record each as a task in [tasks.md](../../../../spec/tasks.md) with the tester's reference, the evidence, and the
   severity they gave. A finding that is disputed stays recorded as disputed, with the reason.
2. Fix with a test that fails first. Where the fix is a rule, add it to the threat model's gap column and close it
   there only when the retest passes.
3. Do not mark WPM-T201 done until the report is in hand, every finding has an owner, and a retest is complete. Update
   the [readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) and the gates list (WPM-T203) in the same change.
4. Keep the report out of the repository if it holds anything exploitable; link to where it is held.

## What a clean report does and does not mean

A test with no findings shows that these testers, in this window, with this scope and these identities, found nothing.
It does not show the absence of flaws, it does not cover a configuration you changed afterwards, and it does not
replace the other gates: an accessibility audit, your data protection impact assessment signed off, and a restore drill on
your platform.

## What this page does not do

It does not name a supplier, set a price or promise a standard. Which scheme or accreditation your sector expects of a
tester is for you to decide.

# For the Chief Executive Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** what is the state of our workforce, what needs my attention, and can we
deliver what we have promised with the people we have?

## What you get

| You want to know | Where WPM answers | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The state of the workforce on one screen | The CEO dashboard: headcount and change, turnover, open vacancies and time to fill, succession gaps, a six-month trend, and the top insights. Sized to fit a tablet without scrolling | [communication-and-leadership.md](../../../../spec/communication-and-leadership.md) (WPM-R48) |
| Which numbers deserve attention | Workforce insights: findings derived from the same figures, each with what to look at next | WPM-R49, same file |
| What we will need, and the gap | Strategic workforce planning: plans as draft worlds, a forecast by transparent rules, headcount and competency gaps, alignment to objectives | [strategic-workforce-planning.md](../../../../spec/strategic-workforce-planning.md) |
| Whether we can start a programme | Delivery capacity: skill pools, programme demand, partner commitments, which pool is the constraint, a start check | [delivery-capacity.md](../../../../spec/delivery-capacity.md) |
| Who could step into key roles | Succession plans and the succession gap on the dashboard (key-person risk analysis is planned, not built) | [talent-development.md](../../../../spec/talent-development.md) |
| How many people we rely on who are not permanent | Fixed-term and contractor engagements, their end dates, funding beside them, and conversion plans | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md) |

## How to read the numbers

- A figure that cannot be worked out shows as missing, never as zero. A trend with too little history says so.
- A forecast is a stated rule applied to stated inputs, not a model. Each result says what it rests on.
- Roll-ups name no one, and small groups are withheld. You will not get a list of individuals from the dashboard.
- Scores advise a person; they do not decide. Nothing in WPM ranks people for dismissal or pay.

## What it will not do

- It is not a payroll system of record, and payroll tax is a stub.
- It does not hold demographics. Equality monitoring exists but is **off** until a deployer records a lawful
  basis and defines the categories.
- The dashboard has not been reviewed by a person using assistive technology.

- Whether to take it past a demonstration. The [readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) says **not ready**

# For the Chief People Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** does this support the whole employee lifecycle, and can I use it without
holding more about people than I should?

## What you get

| Stage | What WPM holds | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hiring | Requisitions, an applicant pipeline, a candidate pool, onboarding checklists | [talent-acquisition.md](../../../../spec/talent-acquisition.md) |
| The record | One employment record per worker, the org chart, reporting lines, groups, transfers between organizations | [hr-core.md](../../../../spec/hr-core.md) |
| Self-service | A worker sees and updates their own details, requests flexible working, gives notice, and sees their time off | [self-service-and-worker-requests.md](../../../../spec/self-service-and-worker-requests.md) |
| Working life | Leave, time, shifts, benefits, wellbeing prompts, reasonable adjustments, ergonomic assessments, the anonymous pulse | [hr-core.md](../../../../spec/hr-core.md), [workforce-management.md](../../../../spec/workforce-management.md) |
| Development | Reviews, 360 appraisals, courses through the course registry, assessments, mentorships, development plans, succession, early careers | [talent-development.md](../../../../spec/talent-development.md) |
| Pay | Payroll runs, payslips, salary benchmarking, a national pay scale lookup, job levels | [payroll-compensation.md](../../../../spec/payroll-compensation.md), [pay-scales.md](../../../../spec/pay-scales.md) |
| Non-permanent staff | End dates by basis, extensions, status assessments, conversion plans decided by a person, funding beside the contract end | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md) |
| Leaving | Resignation with a notice period, a last-day handover, retention per record kind, erasure | [joiners-and-leavers.md](../../../../spec/joiners-and-leavers.md) |

## How it protects people

- **Need to know on reads.** A manager sees their own reports, a worker sees themselves, HR sees what HR needs.
  A signed-in stranger sees nothing about a colleague ([auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md)).
- **No diagnosis is stored.** Sick leave records a kind, not a reason.
- **Special-category features are off by default.** Equality monitoring and workplace health requirements need a
  recorded lawful basis, are voluntary or held by the occupational health role, and show only groups above a floor.
  They are never an input to any score or decision about a person.
- **Scores advise.** Succession readiness, skill gaps and forecasts suggest; a person decides, and decisions such
  as converting a contractor are recorded as a person's decision, never an automatic outcome.
- **The subject can see and erase.** Subject access export and erasure cover the records above, with a ledger so
  a restore does not bring an erased person back.

## Limits

- Not yet built: a user interface for conversion plans and funding, the contingent trend, and the worker's
  "my details" page. Check [tasks.md](../../../../spec/tasks.md) for the current state.
- Translations are machine-assisted; a professional review is an open gate.
- Collective agreements and recognized bodies are research and proposal only ([worker-unions.md](../../../../spec/worker-unions.md)).
- Payroll tax is a stub.

See also [Chief Legal Officer](../chief-legal-officer/index.md) and [Chief Executive Officer](../chief-executive-officer/index.md).

# For the Chief Risk Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** what could go wrong with this system, what stops it, and what has nobody
checked?

## The honest starting point

The [readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) of 2026-10-11 gives the verdict **not ready** for a
high-assurance deployment. It found one blocker by probing the running service: any signed-in person could read a
colleague's sick leave and its free-text reason. That is fixed and tested. The gates only people can close are
still open.

## What you get

| Concern | What exists | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Threats at each boundary | A threat model: assets, actors, boundaries, the control as built, and what is **not assessed** | [governance/threat-model.md](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) |
| Unauthorized reads | A need-to-know guard that classifies every read route; a test fails on an unclassified one | [auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md) (WPM-R114) |
| Tampering and accountability | An append-only, hash-chained audit trail with a verify endpoint; entries hold no reason text or value | [audit.md](../../../../spec/audit.md) (WPM-R115) |
| Sensitive data | No diagnosis stored; special-category features off by default; a small-group floor | [regulatory.md](../../../../spec/regulatory.md) |
| Insecure paths | Production refuses to start with sign-in off, no token key source, a plaintext database connection to another host, or a plaintext remote Redis | [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md) |

| Bias in scoring | An equality impact template, and a register of every score with a draft assessment | [equality-impact/register.md](../../../../spec/equality-impact/register.md) |
| A control self-assessment | A checklist with each answer met, partly met, not met, or for the deployer to answer | [governance/assessment-checklist.md](../../../../spec/governance/assessment-checklist.md) |

## Open risks, as recorded

Supply-chain pinning and signing, load evidence, log checks for personal data, shared rate limits across
instances, a least-privilege database role set, and token revocation guidance are open items in the readiness
assessment, each with a task. The tests were written by the author; none is an independent review.

## What only people can do

An independent penetration test, an independent accessibility audit, the deployer's impact assessment signed off,
a restore drill on your platform, and approval of equality impact assessments. The repository states these
as gates and does not mark them done.

| Supply chain | Licence and ban checks with `cargo deny`, version-pinned shared crates, a software bill of materials on release | [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md) |
| Incidents | A runbook of first actions; you add contacts and notification duties | [operations/runbook.md](../../../../spec/operations/runbook.md) |
| Self-assessment | A control checklist: met, partly met, not met, deployer to answer | [governance/assessment-checklist.md](../../../../spec/governance/assessment-checklist.md) |

## Known gaps, as recorded

- No independent penetration test has been done. The tests were written by the author.
- Actions are pinned by tag, not by digest, and images are not signed.
- Rate limits are per instance.
- The application uses whatever database role it is given; no least-privilege role set is provided.
- Token revocation and maximum token age are your identity provider's.
- The content manager's path loads a script from a public CDN without a pinned version or an integrity hash.
- Logs have not been checked for personal data, and the audit trail is not exported to a monitoring system.
- A managed Redis (cluster, sentinel, access-control users) has not been tried.

## What only people can do

Commission the independent penetration test, review the threat model for your environment, run a restore drill on
your platform, and set branch protection on the hosting platform. See the
[readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md), whose verdict is **not ready** for a high-assurance deployment.

what evidence can I show an assessor? This page gathers the governance, risk and compliance material in one place.

# Independent security testing

**The question you are likely asking:** how do we get people who did not write this software to attack it, what should
we point them at, and what do we do with what they find?

No independent test has been done. The [threat model](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) was written by the
same assistant that wrote the software and was reviewed by no one else, and every control it names was exercised by
that author. The [readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) lists an independent penetration test
as a gate only people can close (WPM-T201, **not done**). This page is a brief for whoever commissions one. It is not a
test plan from a tester and it does not replace one.

## What to give the testers

| Item | Where it is | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A deployment to attack | Yours: [deployment guide](../../../../spec/operations/deployment.md) | Production settings with sign-in **on**, a test identity provider, and **synthetic data only**. Do not test against real people's records |
| The source | This repository | A test with the source is more thorough than a black-box one; say which you want |
| The threat model | [governance/threat-model.md](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) | Twenty-four threats, the control as built, and the gaps. Give it to them **after** a first black-box pass if you want to see what they find unprompted |
| The API description | `GET /api-docs/openapi.json` | Every route, with the `Idempotency-Key` on every operation that changes something |
| The sign-in design | [auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md), [operations/entra-sign-in.md](../../../../spec/operations/entra-sign-in.md) | Personas, attributes, and what the policy decides by action only |
| Test identities | You create them | At least: a worker with no attributes, a line manager, a manager outside the chain, HR, payroll, an administrator, and a service peer |

## What to ask them to look at

The author could not check these. Each row names the threat model's own entry, so a finding can be traced.

| Area | What to try | Threat |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tokens | Algorithm confusion, a key set that rotates while requests are in flight, an expired or not-yet-valid token, a token for another audience | T1, T2 |
| Need to know | Every read route as a caller with no attributes and as a neighbour; a route the classification table does not know; a write that the policy allows but the handler should refuse | T3, T4, T6 |
| Privileged attributes | Whether an attribute in a token can be added, replayed or inherited; who can mint one; a shared or long-lived administrator | T24 |
| Injection | Fuzz every parameter, path segment and body field; the erasure and retention statements are built from typed identifiers and were read, not fuzzed | T12 |
| The browser client | Session handling by the interface server, how it exchanges a session for a token, cross-site scripting through stored text, a content security policy bypass, the content manager's page that loads a script from a public network without a pinned version | T13, T14 |
| Outbound requests | Server-side request forgery through any configured URL (key sets, the sibling services, the shared cache) | T15 |
| Limits | The body limit, the request timeout, the rate limits per instance, and the views that load a whole organization's records into memory | T16, T17 |
| Logs | Whether any personal data, token or query string reaches a log | T19 |
| Idempotency keys | A key used by two callers; the same key with a changed body, path or query; a key that is almost valid; a very large body; two requests racing under one key (the claim is reasoned, not raced by a test); whether a stored response can be read by anyone but its caller | new |
| The audit trail | Any way to change, remove or skip an entry; the chain verification endpoint | T7 |
| Backups | Restore from a tampered or wrongly keyed backup; whether an erased person returns | T10, T11 |
| Supply chain | Pinning of build actions, secret scanning, image signing | T20, T21 |

## Rules to settle before they start

Fill these in with your own security and legal teams. None is decided here.

- **Authority:** who signs that the test is authorized, and for which systems and addresses.
- **Window:** the dates and hours, counted in calendar days, and who to call to stop it.
- **Scope:** what is in (the API, the interface, the sign-in flow, the backup script) and what is out (the identity
  provider's own service, your network, anything shared with other systems).
- **Data:** synthetic only. If a tester finds real personal data, who is told and how it is handled.
- **Destructive tests:** whether denial of service, bulk writes and erasure are allowed, and where.
- **Reporting:** the format, the severity scale, who receives it, how long they may keep it, and how secrets they
  find are handled.
- **Retest:** that the contract includes checking the fixes.

## What to do with the findings

1. Record each as a task in [tasks.md](../../../../spec/tasks.md) with the tester's reference, the evidence, and the
   severity they gave. A finding that is disputed stays recorded as disputed, with the reason.
2. Fix with a test that fails first. Where the fix is a rule, add it to the threat model's gap column and close it
   there only when the retest passes.
3. Do not mark WPM-T201 done until the report is in hand, every finding has an owner, and a retest is complete. Update
   the [readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) and the gates list (WPM-T203) in the same change.
4. Keep the report out of the repository if it holds anything exploitable; link to where it is held.

## What a clean report does and does not mean

A test with no findings shows that these testers, in this window, with this scope and these identities, found nothing.
It does not show the absence of flaws, it does not cover a configuration you changed afterwards, and it does not
replace the other gates: an accessibility audit, your data protection impact assessment signed off, and a restore drill on
your platform.

## What this page does not do

It does not name a supplier, set a price or promise a standard. Which scheme or accreditation your sector expects of a
tester is for you to decide.

software with synthetic data. Nothing here is legal advice.

**The question you are likely asking:** what is the state of our workforce, what needs my attention, and can we
deliver what we have promised with the people we have?

## What you get

| --- | --- | --- |

Sized to fit a tablet without scrolling | [communication-and-leadership.md](../../../../spec/communication-and-leadership.md) (WPM-R48) |
| Which numbers deserve attention | Workforce insights: findings derived from the same figures, each with what to look at next | WPM-R49, same file |
| What we will need, and the gap | Strategic workforce planning: plans as draft worlds, a forecast by transparent rules, headcount and competency gaps, alignment to objectives | [strategic-workforce-planning.md](../../../../spec/strategic-workforce-planning.md) |
| Whether we can start a program | Delivery capacity: skill pools, program demand, partner commitments, which pool is the constraint, a start check | [delivery-capacity.md](../../../../spec/delivery-capacity.md) |

- A figure that cannot be worked out shows as missing, never as zero. A trend with too little history says so.

- It is not a payroll system of record, and payroll tax is a stub.

agreements, the retention schedule you adopt, and whether to turn on any special-category feature.

# For the Chief People Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** does this support the whole employee lifecycle, and can I use it without
holding more about people than I should?

## What you get

| Stage | What WPM holds | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hiring | Requisitions, an applicant pipeline, a candidate pool, onboarding checklists | [talent-acquisition.md](../../../../spec/talent-acquisition.md) |
| The record | One employment record per worker, the org chart, reporting lines, groups, transfers between organizations | [hr-core.md](../../../../spec/hr-core.md) |
| Self-service | A worker sees and updates their own details, requests flexible working, gives notice, and sees their time off | [self-service-and-worker-requests.md](../../../../spec/self-service-and-worker-requests.md) |
| Working life | Leave, time, shifts, benefits, wellbeing prompts, reasonable adjustments, ergonomic assessments, the anonymous pulse | [hr-core.md](../../../../spec/hr-core.md), [workforce-management.md](../../../../spec/workforce-management.md) |
| Development | Reviews, 360 appraisals, courses through the course registry, assessments, mentorships, development plans, succession, early careers | [talent-development.md](../../../../spec/talent-development.md) |
| Pay | Payroll runs, payslips, salary benchmarking, a national pay scale lookup, job levels | [payroll-compensation.md](../../../../spec/payroll-compensation.md), [pay-scales.md](../../../../spec/pay-scales.md) |
| Non-permanent staff | End dates by basis, extensions, status assessments, conversion plans decided by a person, funding beside the contract end | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md) |
| Leaving | Resignation with a notice period, a last-day handover, retention per record kind, erasure | [joiners-and-leavers.md](../../../../spec/joiners-and-leavers.md) |

## How it protects people

- **Need to know on reads.** A manager sees their own reports, a worker sees themselves, HR sees what HR needs.
  A signed-in stranger sees nothing about a colleague ([auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md)).
- **No diagnosis is stored.** Sick leave records a kind, not a reason.
- **Special-category features are off by default.** Equality monitoring and workplace health requirements need a
  recorded lawful basis, are voluntary or held by the occupational health role, and show only groups above a floor.
  They are never an input to any score or decision about a person.
- **Scores advise.** Succession readiness, skill gaps and forecasts suggest; a person decides, and decisions such
  as converting a contractor are recorded as a person's decision, never an automatic outcome.
- **The subject can see and erase.** Subject access export and erasure cover the records above, with a ledger so
  a restore does not bring an erased person back.

## Limits

- Not yet built: a user interface for conversion plans and funding, the contingent trend, and the worker's
  "my details" page. Check [tasks.md](../../../../spec/tasks.md) for the current state.
- Translations are machine-assisted; a professional review is an open gate.
- Collective agreements and recognized bodies are research and proposal only ([worker-unions.md](../../../../spec/worker-unions.md)).
- Payroll tax is a stub.

See also [Chief Legal Officer](../chief-legal-officer/index.md) and [Chief Executive Officer](../chief-executive-officer/index.md).

still open.

# For the Chief Security Officer

**The question you are likely asking:** how is this protected, how would we know if it were attacked or misused, and
what has nobody tested?

## What you get

| Concern | What exists | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Threats | A threat model: assets, actors, trust boundaries, the control as built, and what is **not assessed** | [governance/threat-model.md](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) |
| Authentication | Sign-in on by default; production refuses to start with it off or with no token key source; enterprise directory sign-in (OIDC) | [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md), [operations/entra-sign-in.md](../../../../spec/operations/entra-sign-in.md) |
| Authorization | The policy decides by action only; a classified table decides need to know on every read route, and a source-scan test fails on an unclassified route | [auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md) |
| Audit | An append-only, hash-chained trail with a verify endpoint; entries carry no reason text and no value | [audit.md](../../../../spec/audit.md) |
| Transport and browser | Security headers on every API response, an explicit CORS allow-list that fails boot when unset, `no-store` on `/api` | WPM-R73 in [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md) |
| Abuse | Rate limits per caller, stricter for erase, import, export and token routes | WPM-R74, same file |
| Insecure configuration | Boot refuses a plaintext database connection or plaintext Redis to another host, and a missing CORS origin | [operations/deployment.md](../../../../spec/operations/deployment.md) |
| Data at rest | Encrypted backups; the shared cache holds non-personal lookups only and fails open | [operations/backup-and-restore.md](../../../../spec/operations/backup-and-restore.md) |
| Supply chain | License and ban checks with `cargo deny`, version-pinned shared crates, a software bill of materials on release | [production-readiness.md](../../../../spec/production-readiness.md) |
| Incidents | A runbook of first actions; you add contacts and notification duties | [operations/runbook.md](../../../../spec/operations/runbook.md) |
| Self-assessment | A control checklist: met, partly met, not met, deployer to answer | [governance/assessment-checklist.md](../../../../spec/governance/assessment-checklist.md) |

## Known gaps, as recorded

- No independent penetration test has been done. The tests were written by the author.
- Actions are pinned by tag, not by digest, and images are not signed.
- Rate limits are per instance.
- The application uses whatever database role it is given; no least-privilege role set is provided.
- Token revocation and maximum token age are your identity provider's.
- The content manager's path loads a script from a public CDN without a pinned version or an integrity hash.
- Logs have not been checked for personal data, and the audit trail is not exported to a monitoring system.
- A managed Redis (cluster, sentinel, access-control users) has not been tried.

## What only people can do

Commission the independent penetration test, review the threat model for your environment, run a restore drill on
your platform, and set branch protection on the hosting platform. See the
[readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md), whose verdict is **not ready** for a high-assurance deployment.

See also the [Chief Risk Officer](../chief-risk-officer/index.md) and
[Chief Information Officer](../chief-information-officer/index.md) pages.

should we do about the gap?

# Independent security testing

**The question you are likely asking:** how do we get people who did not write this software to attack it, what should
we point them at, and what do we do with what they find?

No independent test has been done. The [threat model](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) was written by the
same assistant that wrote the software and was reviewed by no one else, and every control it names was exercised by
that author. The [readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) lists an independent penetration test
as a gate only people can close (WPM-T201, **not done**). This page is a brief for whoever commissions one. It is not a
test plan from a tester and it does not replace one.

## What to give the testers

| Item | Where it is | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A deployment to attack | Yours: [deployment guide](../../../../spec/operations/deployment.md) | Production settings with sign-in **on**, a test identity provider, and **synthetic data only**. Do not test against real people's records |
| The source | This repository | A test with the source is more thorough than a black-box one; say which you want |
| The threat model | [governance/threat-model.md](../../../../spec/governance/threat-model.md) | Twenty-four threats, the control as built, and the gaps. Give it to them **after** a first black-box pass if you want to see what they find unprompted |
| The API description | `GET /api-docs/openapi.json` | Every route, with the `Idempotency-Key` on every operation that changes something |
| The sign-in design | [auth.md](../../../../spec/auth.md), [operations/entra-sign-in.md](../../../../spec/operations/entra-sign-in.md) | Personas, attributes, and what the policy decides by action only |
| Test identities | You create them | At least: a worker with no attributes, a line manager, a manager outside the chain, HR, payroll, an administrator, and a service peer |

## What to ask them to look at

The author could not check these. Each row names the threat model's own entry, so a finding can be traced.

| Area | What to try | Threat |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tokens | Algorithm confusion, a key set that rotates while requests are in flight, an expired or not-yet-valid token, a token for another audience | T1, T2 |
| Need to know | Every read route as a caller with no attributes and as a neighbour; a route the classification table does not know; a write that the policy allows but the handler should refuse | T3, T4, T6 |
| Privileged attributes | Whether an attribute in a token can be added, replayed or inherited; who can mint one; a shared or long-lived administrator | T24 |
| Injection | Fuzz every parameter, path segment and body field; the erasure and retention statements are built from typed identifiers and were read, not fuzzed | T12 |
| The browser client | Session handling by the interface server, how it exchanges a session for a token, cross-site scripting through stored text, a content security policy bypass, the content manager's page that loads a script from a public network without a pinned version | T13, T14 |
| Outbound requests | Server-side request forgery through any configured URL (key sets, the sibling services, the shared cache) | T15 |
| Limits | The body limit, the request timeout, the rate limits per instance, and the views that load a whole organization's records into memory | T16, T17 |
| Logs | Whether any personal data, token or query string reaches a log | T19 |
| Idempotency keys | A key used by two callers; the same key with a changed body, path or query; a key that is almost valid; a very large body; two requests racing under one key (the claim is reasoned, not raced by a test); whether a stored response can be read by anyone but its caller | new |
| The audit trail | Any way to change, remove or skip an entry; the chain verification endpoint | T7 |
| Backups | Restore from a tampered or wrongly keyed backup; whether an erased person returns | T10, T11 |
| Supply chain | Pinning of build actions, secret scanning, image signing | T20, T21 |

## Rules to settle before they start

Fill these in with your own security and legal teams. None is decided here.

- **Authority:** who signs that the test is authorized, and for which systems and addresses.
- **Window:** the dates and hours, counted in calendar days, and who to call to stop it.
- **Scope:** what is in (the API, the interface, the sign-in flow, the backup script) and what is out (the identity
  provider's own service, your network, anything shared with other systems).
- **Data:** synthetic only. If a tester finds real personal data, who is told and how it is handled.
- **Destructive tests:** whether denial of service, bulk writes and erasure are allowed, and where.
- **Reporting:** the format, the severity scale, who receives it, how long they may keep it, and how secrets they
  find are handled.
- **Retest:** that the contract includes checking the fixes.

## What to do with the findings

1. Record each as a task in [tasks.md](../../../../spec/tasks.md) with the tester's reference, the evidence, and the
   severity they gave. A finding that is disputed stays recorded as disputed, with the reason.
2. Fix with a test that fails first. Where the fix is a rule, add it to the threat model's gap column and close it
   there only when the retest passes.
3. Do not mark WPM-T201 done until the report is in hand, every finding has an owner, and a retest is complete. Update
   the [readiness assessment](../../../../spec/readiness-assessment.md) and the gates list (WPM-T203) in the same change.
4. Keep the report out of the repository if it holds anything exploitable; link to where it is held.

## What a clean report does and does not mean

A test with no findings shows that these testers, in this window, with this scope and these identities, found nothing.
It does not show the absence of flaws, it does not cover a configuration you changed afterwards, and it does not
replace the other gates: an accessibility audit, your data protection impact assessment signed off, and a restore drill on
your platform.

## What this page does not do

It does not name a supplier, set a price or promise a standard. Which scheme or accreditation your sector expects of a
tester is for you to decide.

## How current this is

Written on 2026-10-11 from the specification, not from a run of the software for this page. Counts that change are in
[implementation-status.md](../../../../spec/implementation-status.md), which a script generates. WPM is demonstration
software with synthetic data. Nothing here is legal advice.

# Para la dirección de estrategia

**La pregunta que probablemente se hace:** ¿está nuestra plantilla configurada para servir a la estrategia, qué necesitaremos y qué debemos hacer con la brecha?

## Qué obtiene

| Quiere saber | Dónde responde WPM | Lea |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qué exige un rol | Perfiles de rol con las habilidades requeridas y una competencia mínima, de modo que una brecha se mide frente a un rol y no frente a una persona | [strategic-workforce-planning.md](../../../../spec/strategic-workforce-planning.md) (WPM-R34) |
| Qué necesitaremos | Planes de plantilla como mundos en borrador, varios en paralelo, con supuestos declarados y demanda por departamento, rol y periodo | WPM-R36, el mismo archivo |
| Dónde está la brecha | Oferta proyectada frente a demanda planificada: una brecha de personas y una de competencias, con palancas listadas como sugerencias y su evidencia | WPM-R37 |
| Si sirve a la estrategia | Objetivos vinculados a la demanda: objetivos sin recursos, demanda sin alinear, roles críticos sin banquillo | WPM-R38 |
| Si podemos entregar un programa | Bolsas de habilidades, demanda de programas, compromisos de socios, la bolsa restrictiva, una comprobación de inicio que es una sugerencia | [delivery-capacity.md](../../../../spec/delivery-capacity.md) |
| Cuánto dependemos de personal no fijo | La parte de las FTE que son contratistas y la que es temporal, por separado, y cuánta financiación termina en cada uno de los próximos doce meses | `GET /api/workforce-intelligence/contingent` (WPM-T109, parcial) |
| Qué pensamos hacer cuando terminen los contratos | Planes de conversión: la decisión de una persona de convertir, prorrogar o terminar, con la financiación junto al fin del contrato | [engagements.md](../../../../spec/engagements.md) |
| Qué más está planificado | La hoja de ruta y la lista de tareas abiertas | [roadmap.md](../../../../spec/roadmap.md), [tasks.md](../../../../spec/tasks.md) |

## Cómo leer una previsión

- Es una regla declarada aplicada a entradas declaradas, no un modelo, y cada resultado nombra sus supuestos.
- Con poco historial de plantilla dice `insufficient_history` en lugar de extrapolar.
- Un plan solo guarda personas hipotéticas. Nunca lee ni cambia el registro de una persona.
- Las palancas son sugerencias. Elige quien planifica, y el software no decide nada.

## Límites

- La palanca «convertir personal contingente en fijo» en los planes está especificada (WPM-R63) y aún no está en el código.
- La parte contingente aún no tiene tendencia: necesita instantáneas separadas por base (WPM-T139, no construido).
- La planificación de cadena crítica y de ruta crítica pertenece a project-portfolio-management, no a esta aplicación.
- Aún no hay interfaz de usuario para la financiación ni para los planes de conversión.

Vea también las páginas de la [dirección general](../dirección-general/index.md) y de la [dirección de operaciones](../dirección-de-operaciones/index.md).

# Para la dirección de operaciones (COO)

**La pregunta que probablemente se hace:** ¿tenemos a las personas adecuadas, en el lugar adecuado y en el momento adecuado, y qué se rompe si alguien falta?

## Qué obtiene

| Quiere saber | Dónde responde WPM | Lea |

| Si un equipo puede cubrir una ausencia | Suplentes por persona, el turno de guardia con cambios y recordatorios, y una vista de cobertura que dice con claridad cuándo no hay nadie disponible | [people-directory-and-cover.md](../../../../spec/people-directory-and-cover.md) |
